definition_en: a secret method of voting, or the paper on which a voter marks a choice
core_image: 一只封口的木箱摆在门口，人人把折好的纸片投进去，纸上不写名字
scene: 会场门口摆着一只封口的木箱，代表们排队把折好的纸片塞进缝里。Each delegate folded the ballot and dropped it through the slot of the sealed box.
sceneCN: 会场门口摆着一只封口的木箱，代表们排队把折好的纸片塞进缝里；句中的这个词指「承载个人选择的那张选票纸」（第 2 个义项：选民在票面上作记号、再投入票箱的那张纸）。

senses.title: Voting in secret
senses.titleCN: 不记名投票：不让别人看见你选谁
senses.definition: a system in which people vote secretly, so that no one knows how each person voted
senses.definitionCN: 一种不公开各人选择的投票方式
senses.example: The union decided to use a ballot rather than a show of hands.
senses.exampleCN: 工会决定采用不记名投票，而不是举手表决。
senses.why: The word began as the name of the little ball dropped into a box; the secrecy of that drop became the name of the whole method.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指投进箱子的小球；这种不让人看见的投法，后来成了整套制度的名字。

senses.title: The paper slip
senses.titleCN: 选票纸：承载一个人选择的那张纸
senses.definition: the printed paper on which a voter marks a choice
senses.definitionCN: 投票人在上面标记选择的印刷纸片
senses.example: She folded the ballot and pushed it through the slot.
senses.exampleCN: 她把选票折好，塞进投票口的缝里。
senses.why: From the ball to the paper: the object that carries one person's choice keeps the name.
senses.whyCN: 从小球到纸片：承载一个人选择的那件东西沿用同一个名字。

senses.title: The counted total
senses.titleCN: 投票总数：所有票加起来的数目或结果
senses.definition: the total number of votes recorded in an election, or the result they produce
senses.definitionCN: 一次选举中记录下来的全部票数，或这些票造成的结果
senses.example: He won the ballot by a narrow margin.
senses.exampleCN: 他以微弱优势赢得了这次投票。
senses.why: A ballot is also the count: once the slips are in the box, the word shifts from the container to the sum inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以指计票：纸片进了箱子之后，词义就从容器转指箱内的总数。

senses.title: The right to vote
senses.titleCN: 投票权：投出那一票的资格
senses.definition: the right to vote, or the act of exercising that right
senses.definitionCN: 投票的权利，或行使这项权利的行为
senses.example: Women fought for the ballot for decades.
senses.exampleCN: 女性为争取投票权奋斗了几十年。
senses.why: Possession of a ballot slip implies permission to cast it, so the object came to stand for the right itself.
senses.whyCN: 手里有选票就意味着有权投出它，于是这件实物也代表了权利本身。

senses.title: The list of candidates
senses.titleCN: 候选人名单：供人挑选的那份名单
senses.definition: the list of candidates or measures that voters may choose among
senses.definitionCN: 供选民从中选择的候选人名单或议题清单
senses.example: Two new parties will be on the ballot in November.
senses.exampleCN: 两个新政党将出现在十一月的选票名单上。
senses.why: A ballot lists the choices before it records them; the sheet is both a menu and a tally.
senses.whyCN: 选票先列出可选项，再记录选择；一张纸既是菜单，也是计数表。

senses.title: Drawing lots
senses.titleCN: 抽签：从容器里摸出小球来决定
senses.definition: the old practice of deciding by drawing small balls or tokens from a container
senses.definitionCN: 旧时从容器中摸出小球或筹码来决定结果的作法
senses.example: In the old guild, officers were chosen by ballot from a bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的行会里，执事是从碗中抽签选出的。
senses.why: Before paper, a ballot was a ball; drawing balls from a bowl was the original random method.
senses.whyCN: 在纸张之前，这个词指的就是一颗球；从碗里摸球，正是最早的随机决定法。

senses.title: To hold a ballot
senses.titleCN: 动词：组织一次投票表决
senses.definition: to ask a group of people to vote on an issue
senses.definitionCN: 让一群人就某个问题投票
senses.example: The committee balloted its members on the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会就新规则让成员投票表决。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb of arranging: to ballot is to put the question to a ballot.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为表示安排动作的动词：举行投票，就是把问题交给一次表决。

senses.title: To cast a vote by ballot
senses.titleCN: 动词：以不记名方式投票
senses.definition: to vote by marking a ballot paper and placing it in the ballot box
senses.definitionCN: 在选票上作记号并投入票箱来投票
senses.example: Every delegate balloted before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 每位代表都在中午前投了票。
senses.why: The verb names the act of using the paper, not the counting that follows.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词指使用那张纸的动作，而不是随后的计票。

intro.en: Ballot reached English through French from Italian ballotta 'little ball'. That Italian word is generally traced to a reconstructed Germanic word for a ball; what is clear is the box full of little balls.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语进入英语，法语又借自意大利语中表示「小球」的词。那个意大利词一般追溯到原始日耳曼语中表示「球」的重构形式；可以确定的是那只装满小球的投票箱。

items.en: Italian ballotta meant 'little ball', a diminutive of balla 'ball'. Words for a ball of similar shape exist across the Romance languages.
items.cn: 意大利语中表示「小球」的那个词，是「球」的指小形式。罗曼语各族中都有形状相近的「球」的说法。

items.en: In Venice and other Italian city-states, voters dropped small balls or tokens into a container to record a choice without showing it.
items.cn: 在威尼斯等意大利城邦，投票人把小圆球或筹码投进容器，以记录不公开的选择。

items.en: French borrowed the Italian word as ballotte, and English took the same word from French in the same period.
items.cn: 法语借入这个意大利词，英语又在同一时期从法语借入同一个词。

items.en: The earliest English records show the word as the little ball used in voting; the paper-slip meaning appears considerably later.
items.cn: 英语最早记录中，这个词指投票用的小球；纸片选票的意思出现得晚得多。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the word meant the paper slip and the whole secret method, and the verb followed. The first recorded dates are approximate.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这个词已指选票纸与整套无记名投票方式，动词用法也随之出现。首见年代为大致估计。

note.en: The first group looks similar in spelling or sound; the second group is close in meaning. None of the look-alikes shares the Italian origin.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或读音上相近；第二组意思接近。第一组里的词没有一个是同一个意大利来源。

entries.definition: heavy material used to steady a ship; the ending is different and the source is Germanic, not Italian
entries.definitionCN: 压舱物；词尾不同，来源是日耳曼语，不是意大利语。

entries.definition: a narrative song or poem; it ends differently and comes from Old French, not Italian
entries.definitionCN: 叙事歌谣；词尾不同，来自古法语，不是意大利语。

entries.definition: a form of stage dance; its final vowel is pronounced, unlike the light final vowel of ballot
entries.definitionCN: 芭蕾舞；词尾元音要读出来，而目标词的词尾元音很轻。

entries.definition: a French verse form; it has an extra final letter and a different stress
entries.definitionCN: 一种法语诗体；词尾多一个字母，重音也不同。

entries.definition: the general act of expressing a choice in an election or meeting
entries.definitionCN: 在选举或会议中表达选择的统称。

entries.definition: the count of votes, or a survey of public opinion
entries.definitionCN: 票数统计，或对民意的调查。

entries.definition: a direct vote on a political question, often one about sovereignty
entries.definitionCN: 就政治问题举行的直接投票，常涉及主权归属。

entries.definition: a vote on one specific question put to the whole electorate
entries.definitionCN: 就某一个具体问题交给全体选民表决的投票。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real object behind the word, real compounds and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：词背后的真实物件、真实的复合词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: The original ballot was a little ball: a voter dropped it into a box so no one could see which side it stood for.
normal.cn: 最早的选票是一颗小球：投票人把它投进箱子，谁也看不见它代表哪一边。

normal.en: Ballot box and ballot paper split the object in two: the container keeps the slips, the paper carries the choice.
normal.cn: 投票箱与选票纸把这件东西分成两半：箱子装纸片，纸片承载选择。

normal.en: Secret ballot is the fixed phrase that names the method; adding secret turns the object into a procedure.
normal.cn: 不记名投票是固定说法，加上「秘密的」这个修饰，就把物件变成了程序。

normal.en: The verb ballot means to send a question to a vote, and the prefix re- means to send it a second time.
normal.cn: 动词形式表示把问题交给投票；加上表示「再次」的前缀，就是再投一次。

normal.en: On the ballot simply means that a name or a question has reached the list voters will see.
normal.cn: 「列入选票」这个说法，意思是一个名字或问题已经进入选民会看到的那份名单。

abstract.en: Picture a ball dropped into a dark box: the hand is hidden, and only the sound of one small object falling is heard.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗球落进暗箱：手被遮住，只听得见一个小东西落下的声音。

abstract.en: Secrecy is the whole invention: the box hides the hand, and the paper hides the name.
abstract.cn: 保密正是这项发明的全部：箱子藏住手，纸片藏住名字。

abstract.en: So a ballot makes a choice countable but not traceable: the count is public, the chooser is not.
abstract.cn: 所以它让选择可以计数、却无法追溯：计数是公开的，选择者不是。

examples.en: Citizens cast their ballots before work.
examples.cn: 市民上班前投了票。

examples.en: The ballot paper was folded twice before it went into the box.
examples.cn: 选票纸折了两折才放进箱子。

examples.en: The club balloted its members on the change of meeting night.
examples.cn: 俱乐部就更改集会日期让会员投票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「巴洛特」——把小球投进暗箱，谁也不知道你选了谁 → 无记名投票

root: 经法语上溯到意大利语 ballotta（小球），其更早来源一般追溯到原始日耳曼语中表示「球」的重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one object: a little ball dropped into a box, then the paper that replaces it, then the count and the right that grow out of that paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一样东西展开：先是一颗投进箱子的小球，接着是取代它的纸片，再由这张纸生出计数与权利。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small ball goes into a sealed box, and the choice is counted without being traced.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗小球落进封口的箱子，选择被计数却不被追溯。

branches.en: HIDDEN CHOICE: secret voting and drawing lots both hide the deciding hand inside a container.
branches.cn: 藏起选择：不记名投票与抽签都把做决定的手藏进容器里。

branches.en: ONE PAPER AND THE WHOLE COUNT: the slip carries a single choice, while the total turns those slips into a result.
branches.cn: 一张纸与全部票数：纸片承载单个选择，总数则把这些纸片变成一个结果。

branches.en: RIGHT AND PROCEDURE: the right to vote is exercised through the act of balloting a group.
branches.cn: 权利与程序：投票权正是通过让一群人投票这一程序来行使的。

branches.en: THE MENU: the same word also names the candidates among whom a choice is made.
branches.cn: 选项单：这个词也指供人挑选的候选人名单。

branches.en: CASTING THE PAPER: the verb names the act of marking a ballot and putting it in the box.
branches.cn: 投下纸片：动词指的是在选票上作记号并把它放进票箱的动作。

intro.en: Ballot is a borrowed noun, so its English family grows from compounds and the agent suffix rather than from a Latin root.
intro.cn: 这个词是借入的名词，所以它在英语里的词族靠复合词与表示人的后缀扩展，而不是靠拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no reliable Latin family for ballot; the deeper source of the Italian word is generally traced to a reconstructed Germanic word for a ball. The formations below are English, and the Italian origin is told in the history section.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族；那个意大利词的更深来源一般追溯到原始日耳曼语中表示「球」的重构形式。下面列出的是英语中的构词，意大利语来源已在词源部分说明。

items.structure: ballot + -er (agent suffix: one who does the action)
items.meaning: a person who votes by ballot
items.meaningCN: 投票人（后缀表示「做某事的人」，语义从动作转到施事者）
items.example: Every balloter must sign the roll.
items.exampleCN: 每位投票人都必须在名册上签名。

items.meaning: the act of voting by ballot
items.meaningCN: 无记名投票这一行为（后缀把动词变成表示动作的名词）
items.example: Balloting lasted from morning until dusk.
items.exampleCN: 投票从早晨一直进行到黄昏。

items.meaning: voted by ballot; put to a ballot
items.meaningCN: 已以无记名方式投票的；被付诸表决的（后缀表示过去或被动）
items.example: The proposal was balloted last month.
items.exampleCN: 这项提议上个月已付诸表决。

items.structure: ballot + box (compound: the second element names the container)
items.meaning: the sealed box into which ballots are dropped
items.meaningCN: 投票箱（后一成分表示容器，语义从「票」转到「装票的箱子」）
items.example: Officials carried the ballot box to the counting room.
items.exampleCN: 工作人员把投票箱搬到计票室。

items.structure: ballot + paper (compound: the second element names the material)
items.meaning: the printed sheet on which a vote is marked
items.meaningCN: 选票纸（后一成分表示纸张，语义从「投票方式」转到「承载选择的纸」）
items.example: The ballot paper listed six names.
items.exampleCN: 选票纸上列着六个名字。

items.structure: secret + ballot (compound: the first element names the quality)
items.meaning: a ballot in which each vote is hidden
items.meaningCN: 无记名投票（前一成分表示「秘密的」，语义落在投票的保密性上）
items.example: The union adopted the secret ballot long before the law required it.
items.exampleCN: 早在法律要求之前，工会就采用了无记名投票。

items.structure: ballot + measure (compound: the second element names the question)
items.meaning: a question placed on a ballot for voters to decide
items.meaningCN: 付诸公投的议案（后一成分表示「议案」，语义从投票动作转到被表决的问题）
items.example: Voters rejected the ballot measure by a wide margin.
items.exampleCN: 选民以很大差距否决了这项公投议案。

items.meaningCN: 重新投票（前缀表示「再次」，语义加在投票动作之前）
items.example: The committee had to reballot the question.
items.exampleCN: 委员会不得不就这个问题重新投票。

definition_zh: 投票；表决；选票；投票权；票源
definition_en: to express a choice formally in an election or meeting, or such a choice when it is counted
core_image: 一只手把写好选择的纸片投进箱口，箱子里已经叠了一层纸
scene: 议事厅里，主持人请成员就预算举手表态，长桌前的手臂陆续抬起。Members will vote on the budget by a show of hands after the debate.
sceneCN: 议事厅里，主持人请成员就预算举手表态，长桌前的手臂陆续抬起；句中的这个词指「对议案投下赞成或反对的一票」（第 1 个义项：行使表决权，就某个议题表明选择）。

pos.zh: 投票；表决；选票；投票权；票数
投票；表决
投票通过；投票选出；表决拨款

senses.title: Cast a vote
senses.titleCN: 投票：把选择正式说出口
senses.definition: to express a choice formally, especially in an election or a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 正式表达选择，尤指在选举或会议中
senses.example: Only half the members turned out to vote.
senses.exampleCN: 只有一半成员出来投票。
senses.why: The core act is a declared choice: a person stands on one side of a question and makes that side countable.
senses.whyCN: 核心动作是把选择说出口：一个人站到问题的一边，让这一边可以被计数。

senses.title: One recorded choice
senses.titleCN: 一票：记录下来的单个选择
senses.definition: a single choice recorded on paper or in a machine, or the mark that records it
senses.definitionCN: 记录在纸上或机器里的单个选择，或记录它的那个记号
senses.example: The motion passed by a single vote.
senses.exampleCN: 动议以一票之差通过。
senses.why: One person's act becomes a unit that can be counted, won and lost.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的动作变成一个可以计数、可以争取、也可能失去的单位。

senses.title: The total and the result
senses.titleCN: 票数与结果：所有单位加起来的数目
senses.definition: the total number of choices recorded, or the decision they produce
senses.definitionCN: 记录下来的选择总数，或这些选择造成的结果
senses.example: The vote was close, and a recount was ordered.
senses.exampleCN: 票数很接近，于是下令重新计票。
senses.why: Once units are counted, the count itself takes the name of the act.
senses.whyCN: 单位被数完之后，这个数目本身也沿用了动作的名字。

senses.title: The right to vote
senses.titleCN: 投票权：参与选举的法定资格
senses.definition: the legal right to take part in an election
senses.definitionCN: 参加选举的法定权利
senses.example: The nineteenth-century struggle gave workers the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 十九世纪的斗争让工人获得了投票权。
senses.why: Permission to act is treated as a thing held: you can be given the vote, or denied it.
senses.whyCN: 行动的许可被当作一件可持有的东西：投票权可以被给予，也可以被剥夺。

senses.title: Elect or approve
senses.titleCN: 投票选出或通过：让选择指向人或议案
senses.definition: to choose someone for office, or to approve something, by voting
senses.definitionCN: 通过投票选出担任某职的人，或通过某项事物
senses.example: The council voted him chairman.
senses.exampleCN: 理事会投票选他当主席。
senses.why: The same act can point at a person (choose) or at a measure (approve); only the direction of the choice changes.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作可以指向人（选出），也可以指向议案（通过）；改变的是选择的方向。

senses.title: A formal motion
senses.titleCN: 动议：交给会议表决的正式提议
senses.definition: a formal proposal put to a meeting for decision
senses.definitionCN: 提交会议作出决定的正式提议
senses.example: They passed a vote of thanks to the retiring teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他们通过了一项对退休教师的致谢动议。
senses.why: A vote is not only the counting but the question being counted; the motion carries the name of the act that decides it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不只是计数，也是被计数的问题本身；动议沿用了决定它的那个动作的名字。

senses.title: A bloc of voters
senses.titleCN: 票源：按投票倾向合成的一股力量
senses.definition: the group of people, or the share of the electorate, that votes in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式投票的一群人，或这部分选民所占的份额
senses.example: No party can win without the urban vote.
senses.exampleCN: 任何政党没有城市票源都赢不了。
senses.why: A mass of individual acts is summed into a social force, and the force is named by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 大量个人行为被汇总成一股社会力量，这股力量也用同一个词来称呼。

senses.title: Authorize money
senses.titleCN: 表决拨款：用投票授权一笔钱
senses.definition: to approve money for a purpose by a formal vote
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式表决为某项用途批准款项
senses.example: Parliament voted funds for the new bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 议会表决通过了新桥的拨款。
senses.why: In legislatures the oldest thing voted on is money; to vote funds is to turn a count into an authorization.
senses.whyCN: 在议会里，最古老的表决对象就是钱；表决拨款就是把一次计数变成一项授权。

intro.en: Vote goes back through medieval Latin to Latin votum 'a vow, a wish', from vovere 'to promise solemnly'. The chain is clear; the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词经中世纪拉丁语上溯到拉丁语中表示「誓言、心愿」的名词，其源头是表示「郑重许诺」的动词。词源链清楚；英语首见年代为大致估计。

items.en: vovere meant 'to promise solemnly, to vow', and its supine stem vot- supplied the noun votum.
items.cn: 拉丁语中表示「郑重许诺、立誓」的动词，其词干派生出表示「誓言、心愿」的名词。

items.en: votum covered a promise made to a god and, in later use, an expressed wish or choice.
items.cn: 这个词既指对神明的许诺，在后来的用法里也指表达出来的意愿或选择。

items.en: In medieval Latin, votum was applied to a formal expression of consent in assemblies, which is the bridge to the modern meaning.
items.cn: 在中世纪拉丁语里，这个词被用于会议中正式表达同意的场合，这是通向现代词义的桥梁。

items.en: English has both the noun and the verb from the sixteenth century; the exact first date is not certain.
items.cn: 英语中这个词的名词与动词用法都出现在十六世纪；确切的最早年代并不确定。

items.en: The franchise sense and the bloc sense developed later, and vote of confidence became a fixed phrase in parliamentary language.
items.cn: 投票权义与票源义发展得更晚，信任投票成了议会语言里的固定说法。

note.en: The first group is close in spelling or sound; the second group is close in meaning. One look-alike actually shares the Latin source, and that is noted.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或读音上接近；第二组意思接近。第一组里有一个词其实同出拉丁来源，已在说明里注明。

entries.definition: the power to reject a decision; from Latin veto 'I forbid'. It looks like vote but has a different vowel and a different origin
entries.definitionCN: 否决权；源自拉丁语中表示「我禁止」的词。它与目标词形近，但元音不同，来源也不同。

entries.definition: a solemn promise; from Latin votum, the same source as vote. The vowel differs and the meaning is promise, not choice
entries.definitionCN: 郑重承诺；与目标词同出拉丁语中表示「誓言」的名词。元音不同，意思是承诺而非选择。

entries.definition: fashionable popularity; from a French phrase, not from Latin votum
entries.definitionCN: 流行、时尚；来自法语短语，并非出自那个拉丁名词。

entries.definition: a unit of electrical force, named after an Italian physicist. No connection to voting
entries.definitionCN: 电压单位，以一位意大利物理学家命名，与投票无关。

entries.definition: the paper on which a choice is marked, or the secret method of voting
entries.definitionCN: 标记选择的纸片，或不记名的投票方式。

entries.definition: the counting of votes, or a survey of public opinion
entries.definitionCN: 票数统计，或对民意的调查。

entries.definition: the right to vote in political elections, used especially in historical and legal writing
entries.definitionCN: 在政治选举中的投票权，多用于历史与法律写作。

entries.definition: the right to vote, in formal political language; also a business licence
entries.definitionCN: 正式政治用语中的投票权；也可指商业特许经营权。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin idea of a vow, the real word family and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实存在的「立誓、心愿」这层拉丁含义、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: The root idea is a vow or a wish: to vote is to state a wish solemnly enough to be counted.
normal.cn: 词根的核心意思是誓言或心愿：投票就是把心里的愿望郑重说出来，郑重到可以被计数。

normal.en: The family spreads outward from one act: voter, voting, outvote and voteless all name parts or results of that act.
normal.cn: 同族词都从一个动作向外扩散：投票人、投票、以多数票压过、无投票权，命名的都是这个动作的参与者或结果。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the grammar of choice: vote for, vote against, cast a vote, put to a vote.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出选择的语法：支持、反对、投下一票、付诸表决。

normal.en: In legislatures the object voted on is often money: to vote funds is to authorize a sum.
normal.cn: 在议会里，表决对象常常是钱：表决拨款就是批准一笔款项。

normal.en: The bloc sense adds many people together: the youth vote, the urban vote, the labour vote.
normal.cn: 票源义把许多人加在一起：青年票、城市票、劳工票，都是合成的一股力量。

abstract.en: Picture one raised hand among hundreds: each hand is a unit, and the units are added in silence.
abstract.cn: 想象上百人里举起的一只手：每只手是一个单位，这些单位在安静中被相加。

abstract.en: A vote turns a private wish into a public integer without revealing the wisher.
abstract.cn: 投票把私人的心愿变成一个公开的整数，却不暴露许愿的人。

abstract.en: So the word always balances two things: the single act and the sum it joins.
abstract.cn: 所以这个词始终在两端之间保持平衡：单个动作，以及它所加入的总数。

examples.en: Most members voted for the earlier starting time.
examples.cn: 多数成员投票支持更早的开始时间。

examples.en: The committee put the plan to a vote on Friday.
examples.cn: 委员会周五把这项计划付诸表决。

examples.en: The rural vote proved decisive in the final count.
examples.cn: 在最终计票中，乡村票源起了决定作用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「沃特」——把心里的话郑重说出口，再投进箱子 → 投票

root: 拉丁语 votum（誓言、心愿），源自动词 vovere（郑重许诺），核心是把心愿郑重许下。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act from the hand to the total: a person chooses, the choice becomes a unit, the units become a result, and the result becomes a right, a motion, a bloc or a budget.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作从手边走到总数：一个人作出选择，选择变成一个单位，单位变成结果，结果又变成权利、动议、票源或预算。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wish declared → marked on paper → counted with others → made into a decision.
core.cn: 核心意象：心愿被说出口 → 标在纸上 → 与他人的选择一起计数 → 变成一个决定。

branches.en: ACT AND RIGHT: casting a vote and being entitled to cast one are two faces of the same permission.
branches.cn: 动作与权利：投出一票和有权投出一票，是同一项许可的两面。

branches.en: UNIT AND TOTAL: one recorded choice is a unit, and the count turns those units into a result.
branches.cn: 单位与总数：一个被记录的选择是一个单位，计数把这些单位变成一个结果。

branches.en: TWO OBJECTS OF CHOICE: the same verb can elect a person or authorize a sum of money.
branches.cn: 两类表决对象：同一个动词既能选出一个人，也能批准一笔钱。

branches.en: THE QUESTION ITSELF: a motion is the proposal that the counting decides.
branches.cn: 问题本身：动议就是那个等待计数来决定的提议。

branches.en: THE MASS: many private acts summed together become a social force.
branches.cn: 合成的多数：许多私人动作加在一起，成为一股社会力量。

intro.en: Vote is a short Latin borrowing that carries a large English family: suffixes name the person and the action, while prefixes redirect the act.
intro.cn: 这是个简短的拉丁借词，却带出一个很大的英语词族：后缀命名人与动作，前缀则改变动作的方向。

latinIntro.en: Latin votum 'vow, wish' and vovere 'to vow' supply the base; the Latin participle votivus gave votive, and devotus gave devote.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「誓言、心愿」的名词与表示「立誓」的动词提供基础；拉丁分词还给出「许愿的」与「献身的」两个英语词。

items.structure: vote + -er (agent suffix: one who does the action)
items.meaningCN: 投票人（后缀表示「做某事的人」，语义从动作转到施事者）
items.example: Every voter received a printed guide.
items.exampleCN: 每位投票人都拿到一份印刷指南。

items.meaning: the act or process of voting
items.meaningCN: 投票这一行为或过程（后缀把动词变成表示动作的名词）
items.example: Voting closed at six in the evening.
items.exampleCN: 投票在傍晚六点结束。

items.meaning: cast a vote; approved by vote
items.meaningCN: 已投票的；经表决通过的（后缀表示过去或被动）
items.example: The plan was voted through by a clear majority.
items.exampleCN: 该计划以明显多数被表决通过。

items.meaningCN: 没有投票权的（后缀表示「缺少……的」，语义从动作转到权利的缺失）
items.example: The voteless workers demanded representation.
items.exampleCN: 没有投票权的工人要求获得代表权。

items.meaning: to defeat by getting more votes
items.meaningCN: 以多数票胜过（前缀表示「超过」，语义加在投票动作之上）
items.example: The smaller party was outvoted two to one.
items.exampleCN: 较小政党以二比一的票数落败。

items.meaning: to vote again on the same question
items.meaningCN: 重新表决（前缀表示「再次」，语义回到同一问题上）
items.example: The chair allowed a revote after the recount.
items.exampleCN: 重新计票后，主席允许再次表决。

items.structure: vote + bank (compound: the second element names a stored supply)
items.meaning: a group of voters who reliably support one party
items.meaningCN: 票仓（后一成分表示「储备」，语义从单票转到稳定的一群支持者）
items.example: The party treated the town as a safe vote bank.
items.exampleCN: 该党把这座城镇当作稳固的票仓。

items.structure: vote + share (compound: the second element names a portion)
items.meaning: the percentage of all votes that a party receives
items.meaningCN: 得票率（后一成分表示「份额」，语义从票数转到所占比例）
items.example: Its vote share fell by four points.
items.exampleCN: 它的得票率下降了四个百分点。

latinEntries.meaning: a vow, a wish, a vote
promised by a vow, offered in fulfilment of a vow

definition_zh: 投票人；有投票权者；登记选民；表决者
definition_en: a person who votes or has the right to vote in an election
core_image: 一只手持证件站在投票站门口，身后是排队等待的人群
scene: 投票站入口，工作人员把选票和笔逐份递到进来的人手里。Each voter received one ballot and one pen at the entrance.
sceneCN: 投票站入口，工作人员把选票和笔逐份递到进来的人手里；句中的这个词指「实际到场投下选票的人」（第 1 个义项：亲自到场、把选择投进票箱的选民）。

pos.zh: 投票人；有投票权者
登记选民；统计口径中的选民

senses.title: The person who casts a vote
senses.titleCN: 实际投下选票的人
senses.definition: a person who actually casts a vote in an election
senses.definitionCN: 在选举中实际投下选票的人
senses.example: Each voter received one ballot and one pen.
senses.exampleCN: 每位投票人领到一张选票和一支笔。
senses.why: The agent suffix marks the doer: whoever performs the act of voting is a voter for that moment.
senses.whyCN: 表示施事者的后缀标出动作的执行者：谁在这一刻完成投票，谁就是投票人。

senses.title: The person entitled to vote
senses.titleCN: 拥有投票资格的人
senses.definition: a person who has the legal right to vote, whether or not they use it
senses.definitionCN: 依法拥有投票权的人，无论是否实际使用这项权利
senses.example: Any citizen over eighteen is a voter in this country.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个国家，任何年满十八岁的公民都是有权投票的人。
senses.why: The doer need not act today; the capacity to act is enough to carry the name.
senses.whyCN: 执行者不必今天真的行动；拥有行动能力，就足以带上这个称呼。

senses.title: The registered voter
senses.titleCN: 登记在册的选民
senses.definition: a person whose name appears on the official list of those allowed to vote
senses.definitionCN: 名字出现在准予投票的官方名册上的人
senses.example: The clerk checked whether the address on the roll matched the voter.
senses.exampleCN: 工作人员核对名册上的地址是否与这位登记选民相符。
senses.why: Registration turns a general right into a listed name, and the listed person is still called by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 登记把一项普遍权利变成一个写在册上的名字，而册上的人仍用同一个词来称呼。

senses.title: The voter in a meeting
senses.titleCN: 会议中参与表决的成员
senses.definition: a member who votes on a motion at a formal meeting
senses.definitionCN: 在正式会议上对动议投票的成员
senses.example: The voter must raise a hand or send a proxy at the union meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 在工会会议上，表决者必须举手或委托他人代为投票。
senses.why: The setting changes from a public election to a room of members, but the act of deciding remains.
senses.whyCN: 场合从公共选举换成一间会员聚集的房间，但作出决定的动作没有变。

senses.title: The shareholder voter
senses.titleCN: 公司年会上的股东表决者
senses.definition: a shareholder who votes at a company meeting, where votes are proportional to shares
senses.definitionCN: 在公司会议上投票的股东，其票数按持股比例计算
senses.example: A large pension fund can be the deciding voter at the annual meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 一家大型养老基金可能在年会上成为决定性的一票。
senses.why: Property, not citizenship, gives the power here, so the word moves into corporate governance.
senses.whyCN: 这里赋予权力的是财产而不是公民身份，于是这个词进入了公司治理。

senses.title: The voter as a statistic
senses.titleCN: 统计口径中的选民单位
senses.definition: a person treated as a unit in surveys, models or turnout data
senses.definitionCN: 在民调、模型或投票率数据中被当作一个单位的人
senses.example: Analysts treat the voter as a number to be modelled, not a person to be met.
senses.exampleCN: 分析者把这些选民当作可以建模的数字，而不是可以见面的人。
senses.why: Surveys turn people into categories; the singular label then stands for a type in a dataset.
senses.whyCN: 民调把人变成类别；这个单数称呼于是代表数据集里的一个类型。

senses.title: The voter in a compound
senses.titleCN: 复合词里按行为划分的选民类型
senses.definition: a kind of voter named by a modifier, such as a swing voter or a likely voter
senses.definitionCN: 由修饰语限定出的某类选民，如摇摆选民或可能投票的选民
senses.example: The swing voter decides the seat, not the party loyalist.
senses.exampleCN: 决定这个席位的是摇摆选民，而不是政党铁杆。
senses.why: Compounds narrow the word to a kind of behaviour, and the head noun still names the person.
senses.whyCN: 复合词把词义收窄到某种行为，而中心名词仍然指人。

senses.title: The first-time voter
senses.titleCN: 第一次投票的人
senses.definition: a person voting for the first time, often treated as a distinct social group
senses.definitionCN: 第一次参加投票的人，常被当作一个独特的社会群体
senses.example: The first-time voter stood in line with her parents.
senses.exampleCN: 这位首次投票者跟父母一起排队。
senses.why: A milestone creates a new social role, and English marks it by attaching a modifier to the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 一个人生节点造出新的社会角色，英语就在同一个名词前加修饰语来标记它。

intro.en: Voter is vote plus the agent suffix -er. The base goes back through medieval Latin to Latin votum 'a vow, a wish'; the first English date is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词由「投票」加上表示施事者的后缀构成。基础词经中世纪拉丁语上溯到拉丁语中表示「誓言、心愿」的名词；英语首见年代为大致估计。

items.en: votum meant 'a vow, a wish', and in later Latin it also covered a formal expression of consent.
items.cn: 拉丁语中这个词意为「誓言、心愿」，在后来的拉丁语里也指正式表达同意。

items.en: English vote appears in the sixteenth century as both noun and verb.
items.cn: 英语中这个词的名词与动词用法都出现在十六世纪。

items.en: The suffix -er, from Old English -ere, was added to the verb to name the person who performs it.
items.cn: 来自古英语的表示施事者的后缀，加在动词之后，用来命名执行动作的人。

items.en: As suffrage widened, the word became common in laws, newspapers and political debate.
items.cn: 随着选举权扩大，这个词在法律、报纸与政治辩论中变得常见。

items.en: Twentieth-century polling made the word a statistical category as well as a description of a person.
items.cn: 二十世纪的民意调查让这个词既是人的描述，也成了一个统计类别。

note.en: The first group shares spelling or sound with voter; the second group names people who are close in role. Differences in origin are stated where they matter.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或读音上与目标词相近；第二组是角色接近的人。来源不同之处都已说明。

entries.definition: a devoted follower or enthusiast; from votum, but it names devotion rather than election
entries.definitionCN: 虔诚的追随者或热衷者；同出那个拉丁名词，但命名的是虔诚，而不是选举。

entries.definition: given or offered in fulfilment of a vow; an adjective, not a person
entries.definitionCN: 为还愿而献上的；是形容词，不指人。

entries.definition: the power to forbid a decision; from Latin veto 'I forbid', with a different vowel and origin
entries.definitionCN: 否决权；源自拉丁语中表示「我禁止」的词，元音与来源都不同。

entries.definition: without the right to vote; it describes a condition, not a person
entries.definitionCN: 没有投票权的；描述一种状况，而不是一个人。

entries.definition: a person with the right to vote in an election; also a member of an electoral college
entries.definitionCN: 在选举中有投票权的人；也可指选举团的成员。

entries.definition: a person represented by an elected official
entries.definitionCN: 由民选官员所代表的人。

entries.definition: a person who votes by ballot; rare outside formal or historical writing
entries.definitionCN: 以无记名方式投票的人；在正式或历史写作之外很少使用。

entries.definition: a person who takes part in an activity; broader than voter and not tied to elections
entries.definitionCN: 参加某项活动的人；比目标词宽泛，也不限于选举。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real agent suffix, the real plural forms and the real compounds built on this noun.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的施事后缀、真实的复数形式，以及由这个名词构成的真实复合词。

normal.en: The suffix means 'one who does': add it to the verb and the doer appears.
normal.cn: 那个后缀的意思是「做某事的人」：加在动词后面，执行者就出现了。

normal.en: The plural adds -s and the possessive adds an apostrophe: voters, voter's, voters'.
normal.cn: 复数加一个表示复数的词尾，所有格加一个撇号：选民、选民的、选民们的。

normal.en: Registered voter and eligible voter separate two ideas: a name on the roll, and a legal right.
normal.cn: 「登记选民」与「合格选民」分开两层意思：名册上的名字，和法律上的资格。

normal.en: Swing voter and likely voter narrow the crowd to a behaviour: the one who may change side, the one who will probably show up.
normal.cn: 「摇摆选民」与「可能投票的选民」把人群收窄到某种行为：可能改换立场的人，和大概会到场的人。

normal.en: Voter turnout adds a second noun to measure how many of these people actually appear.
normal.cn: 「选民投票率」再加一个名词，用来衡量这些人里究竟有多少人真的出现。

abstract.en: Picture one person in a long line: the line is made of single hands, each holding one folded paper.
abstract.cn: 想象长队里的一个人：整条队由一只只手组成，每只手捏着一张折好的纸。

abstract.en: The word can zoom in to a citizen or zoom out to a number in a table.
abstract.cn: 这个词既能拉近到一个公民，也能拉远到表格里的一个数字。

abstract.en: So a voter is a right that has become a person, and a person that data can count.
abstract.cn: 所以选民是一项权利变成了一个人，也是数据可以计数的人。

examples.en: A voter may bring a friend to help read the ballot.
examples.cn: 投票人可以带一位朋友帮忙读选票。

examples.en: The registered voter list was checked twice before the election.
examples.cn: 登记选民名册在选举前核对了两次。

examples.en: Turnout among first-time voters rose sharply this year.
examples.cn: 今年首次投票者的投票率大幅上升。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「沃特」加「人」——把心愿郑重说出口的那个人 → 投票人

root: 由表示「投票」的动词加上表示施事者的后缀构成；基础词出自拉丁语 votum（誓言、心愿）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from one acting person to a legal right, a listed name, a meeting member, a shareholder, a statistic and a labelled type.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个正在行动的人出发，走向法定资格、名册上的名字、会议成员、股东、统计单位与被贴标签的类型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person → one right → one name on a roll → one unit in a count.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人 → 一项权利 → 名册上的一个名字 → 计数里的一个单位。

branches.en: THE PERSON AND THE NUMBER: an individual acting, and the same individual counted as a statistical unit.
branches.cn: 人与数字：一个正在行动的个人，以及被当作统计单位的同一个人。

branches.en: RIGHT AND RECORD: entitlement in law, and the name that proves it on the roll.
branches.cn: 权利与记录：法律上的资格，以及名册上证明这项资格的名字。

branches.en: TWO ROOMS, TWO SOURCES OF POWER: a member's hand in a meeting, a shareholder's stake in a company.
branches.cn: 两间会场，两种权力来源：会议里成员的手，与公司里股东的股份。

branches.en: BEHAVIOUR TYPE: compounds label how a voter behaves rather than who a voter is.
branches.cn: 行为类型：复合词标记的是选民如何行动，而不是选民是谁。

branches.en: FIRST TIME: a new role created by a first act of voting.
branches.cn: 第一次：第一次投票这一动作造出一个新的角色。

intro.en: Voter is built with the agent suffix on a Latin-derived verb, and the same pieces also build a plural, a negative and several compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁来源的动词加上表示施事者的后缀构成；同样的构件还能造出复数、否定形式与若干复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin votum 'vow, wish' and vovere 'to vow' underlie the base; the English suffix -er names the person who carries out the act.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「誓言、心愿」的名词与表示「立誓」的动词构成基础；英语的施事后缀命名执行动作的人。

items.structure: vote + -er (agent suffix: one who does the action)
items.meaningCN: 投票人（后缀表示「做某事的人」，语义从动作转到施事者）
items.example: Every voter received a printed guide.
items.exampleCN: 每位投票人都拿到一份印刷指南。

items.meaning: more than one person who votes
items.meaningCN: 多位投票人（词尾表示复数，语义从单个人扩展到一群人）
items.example: Voters lined up before the doors opened.
items.exampleCN: 投票人在开门前排起了队。

items.meaning: the act or process of voting
items.meaningCN: 投票这一行为或过程（后缀把动词变成表示动作的名词）
items.example: Voting continued until late in the evening.
items.exampleCN: 投票一直持续到深夜。

items.meaningCN: 没有投票权的（后缀表示「缺少……的」，语义从动作转到权利的缺失）
items.example: The voteless workers demanded representation.
items.exampleCN: 没有投票权的工人要求获得代表权。

items.meaning: a person who does not vote
items.meaningCN: 不投票者（前缀表示否定，语义从投票人反转为不投票的人）
items.example: Nonvoters were the largest group in the survey.
items.exampleCN: 不投票者是这次调查中最大的一群。

items.structure: swing + voter (compound: the first element names the behaviour)
items.meaning: a voter who may change which party they support
items.meaningCN: 摇摆选民（前一成分表示「摇摆」，语义落在立场的可变性上）
items.example: The swing voter decided the seat.
items.exampleCN: 摇摆选民决定了这个席位。

items.structure: likely + voter (compound: the first element names probability)
items.meaning: a voter judged likely to turn out
items.meaningCN: 可能投票的选民（前一成分表示「很可能的」，语义落在到场概率上）
items.example: The poll reported only likely voters.
items.exampleCN: 这次民调只统计可能投票的选民。

items.structure: voter + turnout (compound: the second element names attendance)
items.meaning: the number or percentage of voters who actually vote
items.meaningCN: 选民投票率（后一成分表示「到场人数」，语义从人转到参选比例）
items.example: Voter turnout reached a record high.
items.exampleCN: 选民投票率创下新高。

latinEntries.meaning: a vow, a wish, a vote
promised by a vow, offered in fulfilment of a vow

definition_zh: 投票；表决；选举投票；投票行为
definition_en: the act or process of casting a vote, or the occasion on which votes are cast
core_image: 一张长桌前排着队，人们依次在纸上画下记号，桌角的箱子里纸片越叠越高
scene: 会议室里，成员们逐一在纸片上画勾，然后把纸对折交给记录员。Voting will continue until one option wins a clear majority.
sceneCN: 会议室里，成员们逐一在纸片上画勾，然后把纸对折交给记录员；句中的这个词指「把选择正式投出的整个过程」（第 1 个义项：投下选票、表达选择的行为）。

pos.zh: 投票；表决（不可数）
投票的；与投票有关的
投票（现在分词与动名词形式）

senses.title: The act of casting a vote
senses.titleCN: 投票行为：把选择投出去的过程
senses.definition: the act of expressing a choice by casting a vote
senses.definitionCN: 通过投出选票来表达选择的行为
senses.example: Voting is the moment when a private opinion becomes a public count.
senses.exampleCN: 投票正是私下意见变成公开计数的那一刻。
senses.why: The -ing form names the activity as a process rather than a single finished act.
senses.whyCN: 这个动名词形式把动作当作一个过程来命名，而不是一个已经完成的单次动作。

senses.title: An election event
senses.titleCN: 选举投票：有日期与地点的整个活动
senses.definition: the occasion or period during which an election is held
senses.definitionCN: 举行选举的那段时间或那场活动
senses.example: Voting in the district was delayed by heavy snow.
senses.exampleCN: 该选区的选举投票因大雪推迟。
senses.why: A process stretched over a day becomes an event with a time and a place.
senses.whyCN: 一个拉长到一整天的过程，就变成一个有时间、有地点的事件。

senses.title: A decision at a meeting
senses.titleCN: 会议表决：对动议作出决定
senses.definition: the formal decision of a meeting on a motion
senses.definitionCN: 会议对某项动议作出的正式决定
senses.example: Voting on the amendment took less than ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 对修正案的表决不到十分钟就结束了。
senses.why: The same procedure scales down from a nation to a committee room.
senses.whyCN: 同一套程序可以从一个国家缩小到一间委员会会议室。

senses.title: The right exercised
senses.titleCN: 投票权：在固定说法中指受保护的权利
senses.definition: the right to vote, especially in the fixed phrase voting rights
senses.definitionCN: 投票的权利，尤见于「投票权」这一固定说法
senses.example: The court protected voting rights in remote areas.
senses.exampleCN: 法院保护了偏远地区的投票权。
senses.why: The gerund can name the entitlement when it appears in a fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 当这个动名词出现在固定说法里时，它命名的是一项权利而非动作。

senses.title: A method of casting votes
senses.titleCN: 投票方式：把票送出去的渠道
senses.definition: a particular way of casting votes, such as postal or proxy voting
senses.definitionCN: 投出选票的某种特定渠道，如邮寄投票或委托投票
senses.example: Postal voting made it easier for people who could not travel.
senses.exampleCN: 邮寄投票让无法出行的人更容易参与。
senses.why: Modifiers on the gerund name the channel through which the act is done.
senses.whyCN: 加在这个动名词前的修饰语，命名的是动作执行的渠道。

senses.title: Voting behaviour
senses.titleCN: 投票行为：作为研究对象的重复模式
senses.definition: the repeated patterns of choice studied by social scientists
senses.definitionCN: 社会科学家研究的重复出现的选择模式
senses.example: Researchers map voting by age and income.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者按年龄和收入描绘投票行为。
senses.why: A repeated social action becomes an object of study, and the gerund serves as a neutral label.
senses.whyCN: 重复发生的社会动作成为研究对象，这个动名词就成了中性的标签。

senses.title: Used before a noun
senses.titleCN: 作定语：放在名词前说明用途
senses.definition: used before a noun to name the purpose of a machine, place or rule
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，用来说明某台机器、某个地点或某条规则的用途
senses.example: A voting machine must be tested before every election.
senses.exampleCN: 投票机必须在每次选举前接受检测。
senses.why: English freely puts a gerund before a noun, where it works like an adjective naming purpose.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把动名词放在名词前，此时它像形容词一样说明用途。

senses.title: Parliamentary procedure
senses.titleCN: 议会程序：逐项记录选择的表决流程
senses.definition: the series of recorded choices on amendments and bills in a legislature
senses.definitionCN: 立法机关对修正案与法案逐项记录选择的流程
senses.example: Roll-call voting recorded every member's name.
senses.exampleCN: 点名表决记录下了每位成员的名字。
senses.why: Legislatures keep the old procedural sense: a series of recorded choices on amendments and bills.
senses.whyCN: 立法机关保留了古老的程序义：对修正案与法案作一连串有记录的选择。

intro.en: Voting is vote plus the suffix -ing. The base goes back through medieval Latin to Latin votum 'a vow, a wish'; the first English dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词由「投票」加上名词性后缀构成。基础词经中世纪拉丁语上溯到拉丁语中表示「誓言、心愿」的名词；英语首见年代为大致估计。

items.en: votum meant 'a vow, a wish', and later Latin used it for a formal expression of consent.
items.cn: 拉丁语中这个词意为「誓言、心愿」，后来的拉丁语用它表示正式表达同意。

items.en: The verb and noun vote entered English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 动词与名词形式都在十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ing, from Old English -ung and -ing, formed nouns of action long before it became the modern participle.
items.cn: 这个后缀来自古英语的两种名词词尾，早在它变成现代分词之前，就已用来构成表示动作的名词。

items.en: By the Middle English period the form could name either an ongoing action or the activity as a whole.
items.cn: 到中古英语时期，这个形式既能命名正在进行的动作，也能命名整体的活动。

items.en: Voting became a standard attributive word in the twentieth century: voting machine, voting age, voting rights.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词成了标准的定语用词，出现于投票机、投票年龄、投票权等说法中。

note.en: The first group resembles voting in spelling or sound; the second group is close in meaning. Different origins are pointed out where relevant.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或读音上与目标词相似；第二组意思接近。来源不同之处已指出。

entries.definition: the act of forbidding a decision; from Latin veto 'I forbid', not from the voting root
entries.definitionCN: 否决某项决定的行为；源自拉丁语中表示「我禁止」的词，并非出自投票的词根。

entries.definition: the act of making a solemn promise; it shares the Latin source but means promise, not choice
entries.definitionCN: 作出郑重承诺的行为；同出拉丁来源，但意思是承诺，不是选择。

entries.definition: resting or moving on water; only the ending and stress resemble voting
entries.definitionCN: 漂浮在水上；只有词尾与重音跟目标词相似。

entries.definition: the activity of using a small boat; no connection with elections or choice
entries.definitionCN: 划船活动；与选举或选择没有关系。

entries.definition: the act of collecting votes or of surveying opinions
entries.definitionCN: 收集选票或调查民意的行为。

entries.definition: voting by secret ballot, especially in an organisation
entries.definitionCN: 以无记名方式投票，尤指在组织内部。

entries.definition: the whole event of choosing officials, including campaigns and counting
entries.definitionCN: 选出官员的整个活动，包括竞选与计票。

entries.definition: the right to vote in formal political language
entries.definitionCN: 正式政治用语中的投票权。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real action suffix, the real compounds before nouns, and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的动作名词后缀、真实的定语复合词，以及真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: The suffix turns the verb into an activity: what you do repeatedly becomes a process with a name.
normal.cn: 这个后缀把动词变成一项活动：你反复做的事，变成一个有了名字的过程。

normal.en: Before a noun the same form names a purpose: a voting booth is a booth for voting, a voting machine is a machine for voting.
normal.cn: 放在名词前，同一个形式说明用途：投票亭是用来投票的亭子，投票机是用来投票的机器。

normal.en: Voting rights fixes the form to a legal entitlement rather than an action.
normal.cn: 「投票权」这一说法把这个形式固定在法律资格上，而不是一个动作上。

normal.en: Postal voting and proxy voting name the channel; the modifier tells you how the vote travels.
normal.cn: 「邮寄投票」与「委托投票」命名的是渠道；修饰语告诉你票是怎么送出去的。

normal.en: Voting behaviour is the researcher's label for patterns that repeat across millions of people.
normal.cn: 「投票行为」是研究者给千百万人中反复出现的模式贴的标签。

abstract.en: Picture a line of hands moving over papers: one motion, repeated, becomes a process.
abstract.cn: 想象一长串手在纸面上移动：同一个动作不断重复，就变成一个过程。

abstract.en: The word can mean the act, the day, the method or the right, because a process has all of these faces.
abstract.cn: 这个词可以指动作、那一天、方式或权利，因为一个过程本来就有这些面孔。

abstract.en: So voting is time made countable: each mark is a second, and the total is a decision.
abstract.cn: 所以投票是被切成可计数单位的时间：每一笔是一秒，总数则是一个决定。

examples.en: Voting began at seven and closed at ten.
examples.cn: 投票从七点开始，十点结束。

examples.en: The board changed its voting rules last year.
examples.cn: 董事会在去年修改了它的投票规则。

examples.en: Postal voting increased among older residents.
examples.cn: 年长居民中邮寄投票的比例上升了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「沃亭」——把心愿郑重说出口，一遍又一遍地进行 → 投票行为

root: 由表示「投票」的动词加上表示动作的名词后缀构成；基础词出自拉丁语 votum（誓言、心愿）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat voting as an act, an event, a meeting decision, a right, a method, a behaviour, an attributive label and a parliamentary procedure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把这个词分别当作动作、事件、会议决定、权利、方式、行为、定语标签与议会程序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand marks one paper → many marks are added → the sum becomes a decision.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在一张纸上做记号 → 许多记号被相加 → 总数变成一个决定。

branches.en: PROCESS AND PATTERN: one act in time, or the same act repeated across a population.
branches.cn: 过程与模式：时间里的一个动作，或在人群中反复出现的同一动作。

branches.en: TWO FRAMES: an election day, and the channel through which votes are sent.
branches.cn: 两种框架：选举日，以及把票送出去的渠道。

branches.en: TWO ROOMS, ONE PROCEDURE: a committee motion and a parliamentary roll call.
branches.cn: 两间会场，一套程序：委员会里的动议，与议会里的点名表决。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: in a fixed phrase the gerund names what is protected.
branches.cn: 权利：在固定说法里，这个动名词命名的是受保护的东西。

branches.en: AS A LABEL: before a noun the gerund names purpose.
branches.cn: 作标签：放在名词前时，这个动名词说明用途。

intro.en: Voting is a verb plus an action suffix, and the same form freely combines with nouns to name places, machines and rules.
intro.cn: 这个词由动词加表示动作的后缀构成；同一个形式还能自由地与名词组合，命名地点、机器与规则。

latinIntro.en: Latin votum 'vow, wish' supplies the base; the English suffix -ing turns the verb into an activity or a purpose label.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「誓言、心愿」的名词提供基础；英语后缀把动词变成一项活动，或一个说明用途的标签。

items.meaning: the act or process of voting
items.meaningCN: 投票这一行为或过程（后缀把动词变成表示动作的名词）
items.example: Voting closed at six in the evening.
items.exampleCN: 投票在傍晚六点结束。

items.structure: vote + -er (agent suffix: one who does the action)
items.meaningCN: 投票人（后缀表示「做某事的人」，语义从动作转到施事者）
items.example: Every voter received a printed guide.
items.exampleCN: 每位投票人都拿到一份印刷指南。

items.meaning: cast a vote; approved by vote
items.meaningCN: 已投票的；经表决通过的（后缀表示过去或被动）
items.example: The plan was voted through by a clear majority.
items.exampleCN: 该计划以明显多数被表决通过。

items.meaningCN: 没有投票权的（后缀表示「缺少……的」，语义从动作转到权利的缺失）
items.example: The voteless workers demanded representation.
items.exampleCN: 没有投票权的工人要求获得代表权。

items.meaning: not taking part in voting; without the right to vote
items.meaningCN: 不参与投票的；无表决权的（前缀表示否定，语义从投票反转为不投票）
items.example: Nonvoting members still attended the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 无表决权的成员仍然出席了会议。

items.structure: voting + booth (compound: the second element names a place)
items.meaning: a small enclosed place where a voter marks a ballot
items.meaningCN: 投票亭（后一成分表示地点，语义从动作转到进行该动作的场所）
items.example: She stepped into the voting booth alone.
items.exampleCN: 她独自走进投票亭。

items.structure: voting + machine (compound: the second element names a device)
items.meaning: a device used to record votes
items.meaningCN: 投票机（后一成分表示机器，语义从动作转到执行该动作的设备）
items.example: The old voting machine jammed twice.
items.exampleCN: 那台旧投票机卡住了两次。

items.structure: voting + rights (compound: the second element names entitlements)
items.meaning: the legal entitlements that allow people to vote
items.meaningCN: 投票权（后一成分表示权利，语义从动作转到法律资格）
items.example: The law protected voting rights for all citizens.
items.exampleCN: 法律保护全体公民的投票权。

items.structure: absentee + voting (compound: the first element names the voter's situation)
items.meaning: voting by people who cannot reach their polling station
items.meaningCN: 缺席投票（前一成分表示「缺席的」，语义落在投票人不在现场这一情形上）
items.example: Absentee voting is allowed for soldiers overseas.
items.exampleCN: 海外服役的军人可以缺席投票。

latinEntries.meaning: a vow, a wish, a vote
promised by a vow, offered in fulfilment of a vow

definition_zh: 全民公投；付诸表决的议题；公投制度
definition_en: a direct vote in which the whole electorate decides one specific question
core_image: 一张印着一个问题的纸片发到每家每户，答案只有「是」与「否」两格
scene: 市政厅前的公告栏贴出一张纸，上面只有一个问题和两个方框。The referendum asks residents whether the old market should be rebuilt.
sceneCN: 市政厅前的公告栏贴出一张纸，上面只有一个问题和两个方框；句中的这个词指「把某个具体问题交给全体选民表决的全民公投」（第 1 个义项：由全国或全地区选民直接决定一项议题的投票）。

pos.zh: 全民公投；付诸表决的议题
公投制度；公投这一机制

forms.label: 复数（拉丁语式，正式文体）

senses.title: A national vote on one question
senses.titleCN: 全国公投：全体选民直接决定一个问题
senses.definition: a direct vote in which the whole electorate decides a specific political question
senses.definitionCN: 由全体选民直接决定某个政治问题的投票
senses.example: The government promised a referendum on the new constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 政府承诺就新宪法举行全民公投。
senses.why: The Latin gerundive means 'that which must be referred'; a question referred to the whole people is the modern referendum.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁分词形式意为「必须被提交的事」；把一个问题提交给全体人民，就是现代的全民公投。

senses.title: The question put to voters
senses.titleCN: 公投议题：印在纸上的那个问题
senses.definition: the specific question or proposal printed on the ballot
senses.definitionCN: 印在选票上、交给选民回答的那个具体问题或提议
senses.example: The referendum was worded so vaguely that both sides claimed victory.
senses.exampleCN: 公投的题目措辞含糊，双方都宣称获胜。
senses.why: Metonymy: the name of the procedure shifts to the text printed on the paper.
senses.whyCN: 这是转喻：程序的名字移到了印在纸上的那段文字上。

senses.title: The institution itself
senses.titleCN: 公投制度：反复使用的常设机制
senses.definition: the practice or institution of deciding important questions by direct popular vote
senses.definitionCN: 以全民直接投票决定重要问题的做法或制度
senses.example: Switzerland uses the referendum as a regular tool of government.
senses.exampleCN: 瑞士把公投当作常用的治理工具。
senses.why: Repeated practice turns a single vote into a standing institution.
senses.whyCN: 反复的实践把一次投票变成一项常设制度。

senses.title: The result of the vote
senses.titleCN: 公投结果：投票产生的决定
senses.definition: the outcome or decision produced by the vote
senses.definitionCN: 投票产生的结果或决定
senses.example: The referendum changed the constitution overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 公投结果一夜之间改变了宪法。
senses.why: The count produces a decision, and the decision inherits the name of the process.
senses.whyCN: 计数产生一个决定，这个决定又继承了整个程序的名字。

senses.title: A binding referendum
senses.titleCN: 有约束力的公投：结果必须被执行
senses.definition: a referendum whose result the government is legally obliged to carry out
senses.definitionCN: 政府依法必须执行其结果的那种公投
senses.example: A binding referendum forces the parliament to obey.
senses.exampleCN: 有约束力的公投迫使议会服从。
senses.why: Bindingness is a legal quality attached to the outcome, not to the act of voting.
senses.whyCN: 约束力是附加在结果上的法律性质，而不是投票动作本身的性质。

senses.title: An advisory referendum
senses.titleCN: 咨询性公投：只测民意，不强制
senses.definition: a referendum that tests public opinion but has no legal force
senses.definitionCN: 只测试民意、没有法律强制力的公投
senses.example: An advisory referendum tests opinion but cannot change the law.
senses.exampleCN: 咨询性公投只测试民意，不能改变法律。
senses.why: The same procedure can be stripped of legal force, leaving only its informational value.
senses.whyCN: 同一套程序可以被去掉法律强制力，只剩提供信息的作用。

senses.title: A local referendum
senses.titleCN: 地方公投：一个城镇自己表决
senses.definition: a referendum held by a town, city or region on a local issue
senses.definitionCN: 由城镇或地区就本地事务举行的公投
senses.example: A local referendum settled the future of the town square.
senses.exampleCN: 一场地方公投决定了镇广场的未来。
senses.why: The device scales down: a municipality can refer a question to its own residents.
senses.whyCN: 这套做法可以缩小规模：一个市镇也能把问题交回给自己的居民。

senses.title: A petition-triggered referendum
senses.titleCN: 请愿触发的公投：公民自己把问题送上去
senses.definition: a referendum forced onto the ballot by a required number of citizen signatures
senses.definitionCN: 由达到法定数量的公民签名迫使问题进入选票的公投
senses.example: A citizen-initiated referendum put the tax rise on the ballot.
senses.exampleCN: 由公民发起的公投把增税问题列入选票。
senses.why: Direct democracy adds a doorway: enough signatures force the question onto the ballot.
senses.whyCN: 直接民主多开了一扇门：足够的签名把问题强行送上选票。

intro.en: Referendum is a Latin gerundive of referre 'to carry back, to refer'. The chain is clear; its first appearance in English is dated approximately to the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁动词「带回、提交」的将来被动分词形式。词源链清楚；它在英语中首见的年代大致在十九世纪。

items.en: referre meant 'to carry back, to bring before, to refer', from re- 'back' plus ferre 'to carry'.
items.cn: 拉丁语中表示「带回、带到面前、提交」的动词，由表示「向后」的前缀加表示「携带」的词根构成。

items.en: The neuter gerundive referendum meant 'that which must be referred or brought before an assembly'.
items.cn: 这个中性分词形式意为「必须被提交、必须被带到议事机构面前的事」。

items.en: Swiss cantons used popular votes on specific questions from the sixteenth century, giving the Latin word a practical home.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，瑞士各州就针对具体问题举行民众投票，给这个拉丁词提供了实际使用的土壤。

items.en: French revolutionaries used the word in its modern political sense, and English adopted it in the nineteenth century; the first record is approximate.
items.cn: 法国革命者把这个词用于现代政治意义，英语在十九世纪把它借入；最早记录为大致年代。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word spread to national constitutions, local government and citizen initiatives.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词扩展到国家宪法、地方政府与公民发起的程序之中。

note.en: The first group shares the same Latin root or the same word family; the second group names closely related democratic devices.
note.cn: 第一组同出拉丁词根或属于同一词族；第二组是关系很近的民主程序名称。

entries.definition: the Latin-style plural of referendum; it is the same word, not a different one
entries.definitionCN: 目标词的拉丁语式复数；它是同一个词，不是另一个词。

entries.definition: pointing to something else; it shares the carrying root but is an adjective
entries.definitionCN: 指涉其他事物的；同出「携带」这个词根，但是形容词。

entries.definition: the act of sending someone to another place or person
entries.definitionCN: 把某人转介到另一处或另一人那里的行为。

entries.definition: an official who judges a game; the root means 'one to whom something is referred'
entries.definitionCN: 裁判；词根意为「某事被提交给其裁决的人」。

entries.definition: a direct vote on a political question, often used for controversial or symbolic issues
entries.definitionCN: 就政治问题举行的直接投票，常用于有争议或象征性的议题。

entries.definition: the paper on which a choice is marked, or the secret method of voting
entries.definitionCN: 标记选择的纸片，或不记名的投票方式。

entries.definition: the counting of votes, or a survey of public opinion
entries.definitionCN: 票数统计，或对民意的调查。

entries.definition: a procedure by which citizens propose a law themselves
entries.definitionCN: 由公民自行提出法律草案的程序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces of carrying back, the real Swiss practice and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实存在的「带回、提交」这组拉丁构件、真实的瑞士实践，以及真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: The core Latin verb means 'carry back': a question is carried back from the government to the people.
normal.cn: 核心的拉丁动词意为「带回」：一个问题从政府手里被带回人民手里。

normal.en: The gerundive ending means 'must be': the word literally names a thing that must be referred.
normal.cn: 那个分词词尾意为「必须被……」：这个词字面上命名一件必须被提交的事。

normal.en: Hold a referendum and call a referendum are the fixed phrases for starting one.
normal.cn: 「举行公投」与「要求举行公投」是启动一次公投的固定说法。

normal.en: Binding and advisory split the results in two: one must be obeyed, one only informs.
normal.cn: 「有约束力的」与「咨询性的」把结果分成两类：一种必须服从，一种只提供信息。

normal.en: The plural has two accepted shapes, the English-style one and the Latin-style one.
normal.cn: 复数有两种被接受的形态：英语式的一种与拉丁语式的一种。

abstract.en: Picture a single sheet of paper travelling from a town hall to every kitchen table.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸从市政厅出发，走到每一张厨房桌子上。

abstract.en: The whole device is a return path: power sends a question out, and the answers come back.
abstract.cn: 整套做法是一条回流路径：权力把问题送出去，答案再送回来。

abstract.en: So a referendum is a decision handed back to the many, one box at a time.
abstract.cn: 所以全民公投是把决定交还给众人，一次一个方框地交还。

examples.en: The city held a referendum on the new library.
examples.cn: 该市就新图书馆举行了公投。

examples.en: A binding referendum would settle the question for good.
examples.cn: 有约束力的公投将彻底解决这个问题。

examples.en: The petition gathered enough names to force a referendum.
examples.cn: 请愿收集到足够的名字，迫使举行公投。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞弗伦登」——把问题送回给全体人民，让他们画勾 → 全民公投

root: 拉丁语 referendum 是 referre（带回、提交）的将来被动分词，字面意为「必须被提交表决的事」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one sheet of paper: the whole national vote, the question printed on it, the institution, the result, and the legal shapes the result can take.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一张纸展开：整场全国投票、印在纸上的问题、这套制度、投票结果，以及结果可以采取的法律形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a question is carried back from power to the people, and the answer returns as a decision.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个问题从权力手里被带回人民手里，答案再作为一个决定返回。

branches.en: ONE VOTE AND A STANDING TOOL: a single national poll, and the institution built by repeating it.
branches.cn: 一次投票与一项常设工具：单场全国投票，与反复举行后形成的制度。

branches.en: THE TEXT AND THE DOORWAY: the question on the paper, and the petition that puts it there.
branches.cn: 文本与入口：纸上的那个问题，以及把它送上选票的请愿。

branches.en: OUTCOME WITH OR WITHOUT FORCE: a decision that binds, or one that only advises.
branches.cn: 结果有无强制力：一个必须服从的决定，或一个只提供意见的结果。

branches.en: BINDING FORCE: the legal quality that makes the result obligatory.
branches.cn: 约束力：使结果必须被执行的那种法律性质。

branches.en: THE LOCAL SCALE: the same device used by a town.
branches.cn: 地方尺度：同一套做法被一个城镇使用。

intro.en: Referendum is built from the Latin verb referre, and the same carrying root also builds refer, transfer, prefer and confer.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁动词「带回、提交」构成；同一个表示「携带」的词根还能构成提交、转移、偏爱、商议等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ferre 'to carry' is the root, re- 'back' is the prefix, and the gerundive suffix -endum marks 'that which must be done'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「携带」的词根是核心，表示「向后」的前缀指出方向，那个分词词尾标记「必须被做的事」。

items.structure: referre (to carry back) + -ndum (gerundive suffix: that which must be done)
items.meaning: that which must be referred to the people
items.meaningCN: 必须被提交给人民表决的事（分词词尾表示「必须被……的」，语义从动作转到被提交的议题）
items.example: The referendum must be held before the end of the year.
items.exampleCN: 这场公投必须在年底之前举行。

items.meaning: to send back, to mention, to direct attention
items.meaningCN: 送回；提及；把注意力引向（前缀表示「向后」，词根表示「携带」）
items.example: The doctor referred him to a specialist.
items.exampleCN: 医生把他转介给一位专科医生。

items.meaning: the act of sending someone to another person or place
items.meaningCN: 转介；提交（后缀把动词变成表示行为的名词）
items.example: The referral arrived after the first test.
items.exampleCN: 转介单在第一次检查之后才送到。

items.meaning: the act of mentioning, or a source consulted
items.meaningCN: 提及；参照；参考来源（后缀把动词变成表示状态或结果的名词）
items.example: The report makes no reference to the earlier study.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告没有提及早先那项研究。

items.structure: refer + -ee (suffix: the person who receives the action)
items.meaning: a person to whom a dispute is referred; an official in a game
items.meaningCN: 被提交裁决的人；比赛裁判（后缀表示动作的承受者）
items.example: The referee stopped the match early.
items.exampleCN: 裁判提前结束了比赛。

items.meaningCN: 指涉的；参照的（后缀把动词变成形容词，语义从动作转到指涉关系）
items.example: A pronoun is a referential word.
items.exampleCN: 代词是一种指涉性的词。

items.meaning: to carry from one place to another
items.meaningCN: 转移；调任（前缀表示「越过」，词根表示「携带」，语义落在跨越方向上）
items.example: They transferred the files to a new office.
items.exampleCN: 他们把档案转移到新办公室。

items.meaning: to value one thing above another
items.meaningCN: 更喜欢；宁愿（前缀表示「在前」，词根表示「携带」，语义落在把某物提到前面）
items.example: I prefer the earlier train.
items.exampleCN: 我更喜欢早一班的那趟火车。

items.meaning: to discuss with others; to grant an honour
items.meaningCN: 商议；授予（前缀表示「共同」，词根表示「携带」，语义落在把意见带到一起）
items.example: The judges conferred before announcing the winner.
items.exampleCN: 评委们在宣布胜者之前先进行了商议。

latinEntries.meaning: to carry back, to bring before, to refer

definition_zh: 政党；政党组织；选举中的竞争方；执政党或在野党
definition_en: an organized group of people who share political aims and compete in elections to win power
core_image: 一间挂满标语的办公室，几个人围着名单分工，把散开的意见拧成一支能推上选举台的队伍
scene: 总部墙上贴满各区联络人的名单，志愿者按门牌分片，把零散的支持登记成册。The political party opened a branch office in every district before the election.
sceneCN: 总部墙上贴满各区联络人的名单，志愿者按门牌分片，把零散的支持登记成册；句中的这个说法指「围绕共同主张组织起来、通过选举争取权力的团体」（第 1 个义项：以取得执政地位为目标的正式组织）。图中可辨识物件：标语、分区地图、登记册、门牌、折叠桌。

pos.zh: 政党；政党组织（可数）
（作定语）政党的；党派的

senses.title: Organized group seeking power
senses.titleCN: 以争取执政为目标的正式组织
senses.definition: a formally organized group of people who share aims and compete for public office
senses.definitionCN: 由一批主张相同的人正式组织起来、为取得公职而竞争的团体
senses.example: Every political party must publish its accounts each year.
senses.exampleCN: 每个政党每年都必须公布自己的账目。
senses.why: The compound joins 'of the city' with 'part': a section of the citizen body organizes itself and aims at the whole.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法把「城邦的」和「部分」拼在一起：公民整体中的一部分组织起来，目标却指向整个城邦。

senses.title: The party apparatus
senses.titleCN: 政党的组织机构
senses.definition: the offices, staff and branches that keep a party running between elections
senses.definitionCN: 在两次选举之间维持政党运转的办公室、工作人员与地方分支
senses.example: The party apparatus was rebuilt from the local branches upward.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党的组织机构从地方分支开始逐层重建。
senses.why: A party is not only a label on a ballot; it is also a building, a payroll and a filing system.
senses.whyCN: 政党不只是选票上的一个名字，它还是一栋楼、一份工资单和一套档案。

senses.title: Competitor in an election
senses.titleCN: 选举中的竞争方
senses.definition: one of the organized sides that voters choose between at the polls
senses.definitionCN: 投票时供选民在其中择一的组织化一方
senses.example: Five political parties contested the same seat.
senses.exampleCN: 五个政党争夺同一个席位。
senses.why: Elections reduce many opinions to a short list of named sides, and each side is a party.
senses.whyCN: 选举把众多意见压缩成一份短短的名单，名单上的每一方就是一个政党。

senses.title: The parliamentary group
senses.titleCN: 议会党团
senses.definition: the members of one party sitting together in a legislature and voting as a bloc
senses.definitionCN: 同一政党的议员在立法机构中坐在一起、作为一个整体投票
senses.example: The party held a caucus meeting before the final vote.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党在最终投票前召开了党团会议。
senses.why: Once inside the chamber, the electoral side becomes a working group with whips and a common line.
senses.whyCN: 进入议事厅之后，选举中的一方就变成一个配有督导、持有统一立场的运作团体。

senses.title: The governing party
senses.titleCN: 执政党
senses.definition: the party that holds office and directs the government after an election
senses.definitionCN: 选举后掌握职位、领导政府的那一个政党
senses.example: The governing party lost three ministers in a single week.
senses.exampleCN: 执政党在一周之内失去了三名部长。
senses.why: Winning turns the competitor into the office-holder; the same organization now answers for the state.
senses.whyCN: 获胜把竞争方变成掌权方；同一个组织从此要为整个国家作答。

senses.title: The party out of office
senses.titleCN: 在野党
senses.definition: a party that does not hold government and watches the office-holders from outside
senses.definitionCN: 不掌握政府、从外部盯住掌权者的政党
senses.example: The party out of office pressed for a public inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 在野的那个政党极力主张进行公开调查。
senses.why: The compound is neutral, so the same words describe the winner and the watcher; only the seat of power decides which.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法本身是中性的，同一串字既能指赢家也能指旁观者，只看权力坐在哪一边。

senses.title: Membership and affiliation
senses.titleCN: 党员身份与归属
senses.definition: the status of belonging to a party, with dues, rights and a shared label
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个政党的身份，附带党费、权利与共同的名号
senses.example: Her party membership dates from her student years.
senses.exampleCN: 她的党员身份始于学生时代。
senses.why: The organization exists only while people carry cards, pay dues and call themselves members.
senses.whyCN: 组织之所以存在，是因为有人持证、缴费并自称成员。

senses.title: Historical party types
senses.titleCN: 群众党与干部党等历史类型
senses.definition: kinds of party defined by how they recruit: mass membership or a small professional core
senses.definitionCN: 按招募方式划分的政党类型：广泛吸收党员的群众党，或人数精简的职业核心
senses.example: Historians contrast the mass party with the older cadre party.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学者把群众党与更早的干部党放在一起对照。
senses.why: As suffrage widened, parties had to choose between enrolling millions and relying on a few professionals.
senses.whyCN: 随着选举权扩大，政党必须在两条路之间选择：吸收数百万人，或依靠少数专业人士。

intro.en: The adjective goes back to Greek polis 'city-state' through politikos 'of the city'; the noun goes through Old French to Latin pars 'part'. When the two were fixed as one label is not securely dated, so the first use is best treated as uncertain.
intro.cn: 形容词部分出自希腊语中意为「城邦」的词，经意为「城邦的、公民的」形容词进入英语；名词部分经古法语上溯到拉丁语中意为「部分」的词。两者何时固定成一个说法，首见年代无法确证，只能存疑。

items.en: Polis named the self-governing city and its citizen body. The word is Greek, not Latin, and it supplies the idea of public affairs rather than of a private household.
items.cn: 这个希腊语词指自治城邦及其公民全体。它提供的是公共事务的观念，与私人家庭相对。

items.en: Politikos meant 'of the city, of a citizen'. Latin borrowed it as politicus, and English political descends from that line.
items.cn: 这个希腊语形容词意为「城邦的、公民的」。拉丁语借入后，英语的形容词就出自这一条线。

items.en: Pars, genitive partis, meant 'part, portion, share'. The accusative partem sits behind the French and English forms.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语名词意为「部分、份、份额」，它的宾格形式是法语与英语形式的来源。

items.en: Partie meant 'part, portion, side', and also the act of dividing. English took it as party, first meaning a part or a side.
items.cn: 这个古法语词意为「部分、份、一方」，也指分割的动作。英语借入后，最初表示「部分」或「一方」。

items.en: By the seventeenth century party could mean a faction or a side in a quarrel. The date when it settled into 'organized political group' is generally placed in the eighteenth century but is not exact.
items.cn: 这个名词到十七世纪已可指派系或争执中的一方。它固定为「有组织的政治团体」的时间，一般认为在十八世纪，但无法精确。

items.en: Political party became a standard label as elections widened in the nineteenth century. Earlier writers used party alone, and the compound's first appearance remains uncertain.
items.cn: 到十九世纪选举范围扩大，这个由两部分组成的说法才成为标准称谓。更早的作者单用后半段，组合形式首见于何时仍不确定。

note.en: The first group shares a spelling stem or a Latin source; the second group holds things that come close in meaning without being the same institution.
note.cn: 第一组共享拼写词干或拉丁来源；第二组是意思接近、但并非同一种制度的说法。

entries.definition: On its own it can mean a social gathering or one side in a dispute as well as a political group. The compound narrows it to the organized body.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时，它既可指社交聚会或争执中的一方，也可指政治团体；加上前面的形容词后，只保留有组织团体这一层。

entries.definition: A portion, a piece or a role. It shares the Latin source with party but never means an organization of people.
entries.definitionCN: 指一部分、一个零件或一个角色。它与前面的名词同出拉丁来源，但从不表示人的组织。

entries.definition: A devoted supporter of a side, often one who will not listen to the other side. It names a person or an attitude, not the institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一方的坚定支持者，往往不肯听另一方的话。它指人或态度，不指制度本身。

entries.definition: The activity of governing and competing for power. It is the field in which a party works, not the party itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指治理与争夺权力的活动，是政党在其中运作的领域，而不是政党本身。

entries.definition: A smaller group within a larger body, often held together by one interest. It is usually narrower and more quarrelsome than a party.
entries.definitionCN: 较大团体内部的小团体，常由某一项利益维系。它通常比政党更窄，也更好斗。

entries.definition: A loose campaign around a cause. It may support candidates but need not contest elections as an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕某项事业形成的松散运动。它可以支持候选人，却不必作为组织参加选举。

entries.definition: A group of states or members acting together for voting strength. It is defined by joint action, not by a membership card.
entries.definitionCN: 为投票力量而共同行动的一群国家或成员。它靠联合行动界定，而不靠党员证。

entries.definition: An alliance of parties formed for a purpose and able to dissolve. A party is a lasting organization; a coalition is a deal between such organizations.
entries.definitionCN: 为某个目的结成的政党联盟，可以解散。政党是持久组织，联盟则是这类组织之间的交易。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek city-state behind the adjective, the Latin 'part' behind the noun, real derived words and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：形容词背后是希腊城邦，名词背后是拉丁语「部分」，再加上真实派生词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Polis 'city-state' gives the adjective: a party deals in public affairs, not private ones.
normal.cn: 希腊语中意为「城邦」的词给出形容词部分：政党处理的是公共事务，不是私事。

normal.en: Pars 'part' gives the noun: a party is one part of the citizen body organized for the whole.
normal.cn: 拉丁语中意为「部分」的词给出名词部分：政党是公民整体中被组织起来的那一部分。

normal.en: The family runs politics, politician, political, politically and partisan.
normal.cn: 同族词包括政治、政治家、政治的、政治上与党派支持者这几个词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the institution: join a political party, form a political party, the ruling political party.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这一制度：加入政党、组建政党、执政党。

normal.en: Its mirror image is the party out of office, which watches rather than governs.
normal.cn: 它的镜像是在野的那个政党，只监督而不执政。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd splitting into two rows of chairs, then each row choosing a name and a colour.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人分成两排椅子，然后每一排给自己取一个名字、挑一种颜色。

abstract.en: A party is a part that behaves as if it were the whole, until the next vote corrects it.
abstract.cn: 政党就是一部分人表现得仿佛自己是整体，直到下一次投票把它纠正过来。

abstract.en: The label on the ballot is the visible tip; the offices and dues are the body underneath.
abstract.cn: 选票上的名字只是露出的尖端，底下的办公室与党费才是它的身体。

examples.en: A political party that cannot raise funds cannot print a single poster.
examples.cn: 一个筹不到钱的政党连一张海报都印不出来。

examples.en: The same political party has governed the country for three terms.
examples.cn: 同一个政党已经连续三次执政。

examples.en: Local members of the political party met in a rented hall to choose a candidate.
examples.cn: 这个政党的本地党员在一间租来的礼堂里开会，挑选候选人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡里提扣·帕提」——先「破立」旧规矩，再「替」人办事，最后「怕踢」出局，正好是一支争权的队伍

root: 希腊语 polis「城邦」经 politikos「城邦的、公民的」进入英语作形容词；名词部分经古法语上溯到拉丁 pars/partem「部分、份」，本义「一部分人」，后固定指政党。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one body through time: a part of the citizens organizes, competes, sits, governs, watches itself and finally takes different historical shapes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一个团体走完一圈：公民中的一部分先组织起来，再参加竞争、进入议事厅、掌握政府、从外部盯住自己，最后分化出不同的历史形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a part of the citizens turns itself into a named body and aims at the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：公民中的一部分把自己变成一个有名字的团体，并把目标指向整体。

branches.en: FORM AND VARIETY: the basic organized group and the historical shapes it takes when recruiting members.
branches.cn: 形态与变体：基本的有组织团体，以及它在招募成员时分化出的历史形态。

branches.en: BODY AND MEMBERS: offices and staff keep it running, while cards and dues keep it populated.
branches.cn: 躯体与成员：办公室和职员让它运转，党员证与党费让它有人。

branches.en: OUTSIDE AND INSIDE: on the ballot it is a competitor, inside the chamber it is a voting bloc.
branches.cn: 门外与门内：在选票上它是竞争方，进了议事厅它就是一个投票集团。

branches.en: IN OFFICE: winning converts the competitor into the body that answers for the state.
branches.cn: 掌权：胜选把竞争方变成替国家作答的机构。

branches.en: OUT OF OFFICE: the same label now marks the watcher rather than the office-holder.
branches.cn: 在野：同一个名号现在标的是旁观者，而不是掌权者。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Greek-derived adjective with a French-derived noun, and each part has its own family of suffixes and related words.
intro.cn: 这个短语由希腊来源的形容词与法语来源的名词拼成，两部分各自带一串后缀与相关词。

latinIntro.en: Greek polis supplies the first element through politikos; Latin pars, partis supplies the second through Old French. Latin politicus is a later borrowing of the Greek adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 第一段来自希腊语中意为「城邦」的词；第二段来自拉丁语中意为「部分」的名词，经古法语进入英语。后来拉丁语又借入了那个希腊形容词。

items.structure: politic- (Greek polis 'city-state' via politikos) + -al (Latin adjective suffix)
items.meaning: of the city, of public affairs
items.meaningCN: 城邦的；公共事务的，语义偏移为「政治的」
items.example: The debate turned political within minutes.
items.exampleCN: 辩论几分钟内就变成了政治争论。

items.structure: politic- + -s (Greek plural ta politika 'affairs of the city')
items.meaningCN: 公共事务的领域，由形容词转为学科与活动之名
items.example: She entered politics at thirty.
items.exampleCN: 她三十岁进入政界。

items.meaning: one who works in public affairs
items.meaningCN: 从事公共事务的人，语义偏移为「政治家、政客」
items.example: The politician refused to answer.
items.exampleCN: 那位政治家拒绝回答。

items.structure: part- (Latin pars, partem 'part') + -y (noun suffix through Old French -ie)
items.meaningCN: 部分或一方，语义偏移为「政党、聚会」
items.example: The party chose a new leader.
items.exampleCN: 该党选出了新领袖。

items.structure: part- + -isan (adherent suffix through French and Italian)
items.meaning: a devoted follower of a side
items.meaningCN: 某一方的忠实跟随者，语义偏移为「党徒、偏袒的」
items.example: Partisan cheers drowned the question.
items.exampleCN: 党派性的欢呼声淹没了提问。

items.meaning: of a part only; hence biased
items.meaningCN: 只涉及一部分的，语义偏移为「不完整的、偏袒的」
items.example: The report was partial and incomplete.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告既偏袒又不完整。

items.meaningCN: 取一份，语义偏移为「参与、分享」
items.example: Guests may partake of the buffet.
items.exampleCN: 客人可以享用自助餐。

items.meaning: the state of sharing an enterprise
items.meaningCN: 合伙关系，语义偏移为「伙伴关系、合伙企业」
items.example: The two firms signed a partnership.
items.exampleCN: 这两家公司签署了合伙协议。

definition_zh: 政党；社交聚会；诉讼或合同的一方；参与人；执行任务的小队；庆祝
definition_en: an organized political group, a social gathering, or one of the sides in a legal or other matter
core_image: 客厅里灯亮到深夜，桌上杯盘未收，同一群人先谈事再举杯，散场时各自站成一伙
scene: 屋顶上串灯亮起来，长桌摆满食物，音乐一响，邻居们陆续上楼。They held a party on the roof to celebrate the new shop.
sceneCN: 屋顶上串灯亮起来，长桌摆满食物，音乐一响，邻居们陆续上楼；句中的这个词指「为庆祝或娱乐把人们请到一起的聚会」（第 2 个义项：围绕一个由头把亲友聚在一处的社交活动）。图中可辨识物件：串灯、长桌、餐盘、音响、楼梯。

pos.zh: 政党；聚会；一方；参与者；小队
（口语）尽情庆祝；参加聚会

senses.title: An organized political group
senses.titleCN: 有组织的政治团体
senses.definition: a lasting organization that contests elections under one name and programme
senses.definitionCN: 以同一个名号与纲领参加选举的持久组织
senses.example: The party won two seats on the city council.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党在市议会赢下两个席位。
senses.why: The oldest extended sense: one part of the citizen body organizes and speaks for the whole.
senses.whyCN: 这是较早的引申义：公民整体中的一部分组织起来，替整体发言。

senses.title: A social gathering
senses.titleCN: 社交聚会
senses.definition: an occasion when people are invited to eat, drink and enjoy themselves together
senses.definitionCN: 邀请人们聚在一起吃喝、娱乐的场合
senses.example: She invited forty guests to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 她请了四十位客人参加聚会。
senses.why: A party is a group of people assembled on purpose; the pleasure is added to the gathering, not to the word's core.
senses.whyCN: 聚会就是一群人特意聚到一起；欢乐是加在「聚」之上的，而不是这个词的核心。

senses.title: One side in a legal matter
senses.titleCN: 诉讼或合同的一方
senses.definition: one of the persons or groups bound by a contract, a lawsuit or a treaty
senses.definitionCN: 受合同、诉讼或条约约束的一个人或一方
senses.example: Each party must sign every page of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 合同每一页都必须由各方签字。
senses.why: Law divides a matter into sides, and each side is a part with rights and duties.
senses.whyCN: 法律把一件事分成若干方，每一方都是带着权利与义务的「一部分」。

senses.title: A participant in an activity
senses.titleCN: 某项活动的参与人
senses.definition: a person or group that takes part in a discussion, an agreement or an event
senses.definitionCN: 参加讨论、协议或事件的人或团体
senses.example: All parties to the talks agreed on the timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈各方就时间表达成一致。
senses.why: To be a party is to hold a part: the participant is one of the pieces that make the event happen.
senses.whyCN: 成为一方就是持有一份：参与人是促成这件事的若干块之一。

senses.title: A small task team
senses.titleCN: 执行任务的小队
senses.definition: a small group sent out to do one job, such as a search or a survey
senses.definitionCN: 为完成某一任务而派出的小队，如搜索队或勘察队
senses.example: A search party set out before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 一支搜索队在天亮前出发。
senses.why: The group is a part detached from a larger body and given a single errand.
senses.whyCN: 这一小队是从较大团体中分出来的一部分，只领一项差事。

senses.title: One side in a quarrel
senses.titleCN: 争端中的一方
senses.definition: one of the opposing sides in a disagreement, especially a public or legal one
senses.definitionCN: 争执中相互对立的一方，尤指公开或法律层面的争执
senses.example: The two parties in the quarrel refused to meet.
senses.exampleCN: 争执双方都拒绝见面。
senses.why: Disagreement splits people into sides, and each side is literally a part standing against another part.
senses.whyCN: 分歧把人分成两边，每一方字面上就是与另一部分相对的一部分。

senses.title: To celebrate
senses.titleCN: 动词：尽情庆祝
senses.definition: to enjoy oneself at a celebration, often noisily and late into the night
senses.definitionCN: 在庆祝活动中尽情玩乐，常常热闹到深夜
senses.example: They partied until the neighbours complained.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一直玩到邻居来抱怨。
senses.why: The verb turns the gathering into an activity: to do what people do at a party.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「聚会」变成一种活动：做人们在聚会上会做的那些事。

senses.title: A group travelling together
senses.titleCN: 同行的一群人
senses.definition: a set of people who go somewhere together as one unit, as in a party of climbers
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个单位一起前往某处的一群人，如登山队
senses.example: A party of tourists blocked the narrow path.
senses.exampleCN: 一群游客堵住了那条窄路。
senses.why: The group is one part of all travellers, moving as a single body with a common route.
senses.whyCN: 这群人是所有出行者中的一部分，沿同一条路线作为一个整体移动。

intro.en: Party comes through Old French partie from Latin pars, partem 'part, share'. The political sense is an English extension of 'side'; the social sense later grew from 'group assembled'. The dates of both shifts are not exact.
intro.cn: 这个词经古法语中意为「部分、一方」的名词，上溯到拉丁语中意为「部分、份」的名词。政党义是英语里从「一方」引申出来的，社交义则从「聚在一起的一群人」发展而来。两次转变的具体年代都不精确。

items.en: Pars, genitive partis, meant 'part, portion, share'. It is the source of a large family: partial, particle, partner, partition.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语名词的属格词干意为「部分、份、份额」。它是庞大词族的源头，包括「部分的」「微粒」「伙伴」「分割」等词。

items.en: Partie meant 'part, portion, side', and also a division or a game. English borrowed it with the sense of a portion or a side.
items.cn: 这个古法语名词意为「部分、份、一方」，也指分割或一局游戏。英语借入时取其「一部分」或「一方」之义。

items.en: By the fourteenth century the English noun meant a part, a side, or a person taking part. The spelling settled as party later.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，英语中的这个名词已表示「一部分」「一方」或「参与者」。拼写后来才固定下来。

items.en: Party could then mean a faction or a side in a public quarrel. The step from 'faction' to 'lasting electoral organization' is generally dated to the eighteenth century but is not certain.
items.cn: 这时它已可指派系或公开争执中的一方。从「派系」到「持久的选举组织」这一步，一般认为发生在十八世纪，但并不能确定。

items.en: The 'social gathering' sense appears in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. It is generally explained as a natural extension of 'a group of people', though the exact date is imprecise.
items.cn: 「社交聚会」这一义项出现在十八至十九世纪，一般认为是从「聚在一起的一群人」这一义直接引申，具体年代不精确。

items.en: In modern usage party covers politics, law, travel and entertainment at once, which is why the single word needs context.
items.cn: 在现代用法里，这个词同时覆盖政治、法律、出行与娱乐，因此单独出现时必须靠语境判断。

note.en: The first group shares the spelling stem or the Latin source; the second group gathers words for gatherings, sides and subgroups.
note.cn: 第一组共享拼写词干或拉丁来源；第二组汇集了表示聚会、一方与小团体的词。

entries.definition: A portion, a piece or a role. It shares the Latin source but never names an organized group of people.
entries.definitionCN: 指一部分、一个零件或一个角色。它与本词同出拉丁来源，却从不表示人的组织。

entries.definition: Incomplete, or favouring one side. It is the adjective built on the same 'part' idea, not a noun for a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指不完整的，或偏袒一方的。它是同一「部分」概念构成的形容词，不是指团体的名词。

entries.definition: A firm supporter of one side, often one who refuses to hear the other. It describes a follower, not the organization.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一方的坚定支持者，往往拒听另一方。它描述跟随者，而不是组织。

entries.definition: A very small piece of matter or of language. It comes from a Latin diminutive of 'part' and has no social meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指物质或语言中极小的单位，来自拉丁语「部分」的指小形式，没有任何社交含义。

entries.definition: Any bringing of people together. It need not be a celebration and carries no hint of music or drink.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们聚到一起的任何场合，不一定是庆祝，也不带音乐或酒水的意味。

entries.definition: An event held to mark a success or a date. It stresses the reason for meeting rather than the meeting itself.
entries.definitionCN: 为纪念某项成功或某个日子而举行的活动。它强调聚会的理由，而不是聚会本身。

entries.definition: A small group inside a larger one, often pushing its own interest. It is narrower and usually more divisive than a party.
entries.definitionCN: 较大团体内部的小团体，常推行自身利益。它比政党更窄，也通常更具分裂性。

entries.definition: One of two or more positions in a dispute. It can be a party's standpoint without being an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 指争执中的两个或多个立场之一。它可以是某一方的立场，却不构成组织。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin word for 'part', the real derived family, and the fixed phrases that keep the senses apart.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中意为「部分」的词、真实的派生词族，以及把各义项区分开的固定搭配。

normal.en: A party is a part of the people: one slice of the crowd organized to act as a whole.
normal.cn: 政党就是人的一部分：人群中的一片组织起来，像整体一样行动。

normal.en: The legal sense keeps the same picture: a contract has sides, and each side is a part.
normal.cn: 法律义保留同一幅图：合同有若干边，每一边就是一部分。

normal.en: A search party is a part cut off from the main body and sent on one errand.
normal.cn: 搜索队就是从主体上分出去、只领一项差事的一部分。

normal.en: The family runs partner, partnership, partisan, partly and partygoer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括伙伴、合伙关系、党派支持者、部分地与聚会参加者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases separate the senses: throw a party, a party to the dispute, the ruling party.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把义项分开：举办聚会、争端一方、执政党。

abstract.en: Picture a cake cut into slices: one slice is taken out, given a name and made to speak for the cake.
abstract.cn: 想象一个蛋糕被切成若干块：其中一块被取出来、起了名字，还让它代表整个蛋糕说话。

abstract.en: Every sense of the word keeps that slice: a slice of citizens, of guests, of a contract, of a crowd.
abstract.cn: 这个词的每个义项都保留着那一块：公民的一块、客人的一块、合同的一块、人群的一块。

abstract.en: So a party is always both less than the whole and loud enough to be mistaken for it.
abstract.cn: 所以一方永远既小于整体，又响得足以被误当成整体。

examples.en: The party has promised to cut the tax on fuel.
examples.cn: 这个政党承诺削减燃料税。

examples.en: He arrived at the party with a bottle of wine and no gift.
examples.cn: 他带了一瓶酒、没带礼物就来了聚会。

examples.en: Neither party may cancel the lease without two months' notice.
examples.cn: 任何一方都不得在未提前两个月通知的情况下取消租约。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「帕提」——把「怕」生冷场的人「提」到一起，再摆上吃喝，就是一场聚会；人一分派，又成了政党

root: 本词经古法语中意为「部分、一方」的名词，上溯到拉丁语 pars/partem（部分、份），本义「一部分、一方」；政党义由「一方」引申，聚会义由「聚在一起的一群人」引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep the idea of a part: a part of the citizens, a part of the guests, a part of a contract, a part of a crowd, and finally the act of enjoying the gathering.
