sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留「一部分」的意思：公民的一部分、客人的一部分、合同的一部分、人群的一部分，最后还有享受这场聚会的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: take one part out of a whole, give it a name, and let it act as a unit.
core.cn: 核心意象：从整体中取出一部分，给它一个名字，让它作为一个单位行动。

branches.en: NAMED GROUP AND TRAVELLING GROUP: both take one part of a larger crowd and move or speak as a single body.
branches.cn: 有名号的团体与同行的团体：两者都从更大的人群中取出一部分，作为一个整体行动或发言。

branches.en: EVENT AND VERB: the gathering is a thing, and celebrating is what people do inside it.
branches.cn: 场合与动词：聚会是一件事物，庆祝则是人们在其中做的事。

branches.en: BOUND SIDE AND ACTIVE PARTICIPANT: a contract binds a side, while a discussion welcomes a participant.
branches.cn: 受约束的一方与主动的参与人：合同约束一方，讨论则欢迎参与人。

branches.en: DETACHED CREW: a small part is cut off from the main body and sent on one job.
branches.cn: 分出来的小队：一小部分从主体上分出去，被派去完成一项任务。

branches.en: OPPOSING SIDE: disagreement splits the whole into two parts that face each other.
branches.cn: 对立的一方：分歧把整体劈成相对而立的两部分。

intro.en: Party is a Latin root plus a French noun suffix, and the same root builds a large English family.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁词根加一个法语名词后缀构成的，同一词根还构成了一大批英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pars, partem 'part' supplies the root; the noun suffix came through Old French -ie from Latin -ia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中意为「部分」的名词提供词根；名词后缀经古法语进入英语，再上溯到拉丁语的名词后缀。

items.meaningCN: 一部分；一个角色
items.example: She read the first part of the report.
items.exampleCN: 她读了报告的第一部分。

items.structure: part + -y (noun suffix through Old French -ie, from Latin -ia)
items.meaningCN: 表示状态或集合体，语义偏移为「一方、团体」
items.example: The suffix turns the root into a countable noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词根变成一个可数名词。

items.meaningCN: 只涉及一部分的，语义偏移为「不完整的、偏袒的」
items.example: A partial answer is better than none.
items.exampleCN: 不完整的答案也胜过没有答案。

items.meaningCN: 部分地；不完全地
items.example: The road is partly closed.
items.exampleCN: 这条路部分封闭。

items.meaningCN: 分享者，语义偏移为「伙伴、合伙人」
items.example: She is my dance partner.
items.exampleCN: 她是我的舞伴。

items.meaningCN: 合伙状态，语义偏移为「伙伴关系、合伙企业」
items.example: The two doctors formed a partnership.
items.exampleCN: 两位医生结成了合伙关系。

items.structure: part- + -isan (adherent suffix via French and Italian)
items.meaningCN: 某一方的跟随者，语义偏移为「党徒、偏袒的」
items.example: Partisan slogans filled the square.
items.exampleCN: 广场上到处是党派口号。

items.meaning: to take a share of something
items.meaningCN: 取一份，语义偏移为「参与、分享」
items.example: Everyone may partake of the meal.
items.exampleCN: 每个人都可以享用这顿饭。

definition_zh: 反对；抵抗；在野阵营；对立立场；对比；天体冲；对手；正式异议
definition_en: the act of resisting or arguing against something, or the side that stands against another
core_image: 两排人隔着一条长桌，一边推、一边挡，桌面中线谁都不肯越过
scene: 会场里两排座位面对面，提案刚念完，前排就有人站起来反驳。The new road plan ran into strong opposition from residents.
sceneCN: 会场里两排座位面对面，提案刚念完，前排就有人站起来反驳；句中的这个词指「来自某群人的抵抗」（第 1 个义项：对某项计划或政策表示反对并设法阻止）。图中可辨识物件：长桌、两排座椅、摊开的提案、举起的手、麦克风。

pos.zh: 反对；抵抗；对立的一方（不可数或可数）
（作定语）反对的；对立面的

senses.title: Resistance to a plan
senses.titleCN: 对计划或政策的抵抗
senses.definition: active disagreement with a proposal, shown by argument, voting or protest
senses.definitionCN: 对某项提议的积极不同意，通过争辩、投票或抗议表现出来
senses.example: Plans for the tower met fierce opposition at the first hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 建塔方案在第一次听证会上遭到激烈反对。
senses.why: The word is built from 'place against': something is set face to face with a plan and pushes back.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「放到对面」构成：某样东西被摆到计划对面，然后往回推。

senses.title: The side out of office
senses.titleCN: 在野阵营
senses.definition: the parties or politicians who do not hold government and argue against those who do
senses.definitionCN: 不掌握政府、专门与掌权者争辩的政党或政治人物
senses.example: The opposition voted against the budget in every committee.
senses.exampleCN: 在野阵营在每个委员会都投票反对这份预算。
senses.why: Parliament seats face each other, so the side without power is literally placed opposite the ministers.
senses.whyCN: 议会席位两两相对，于是没有权力的那一边字面上就被安置在部长们的对面。

senses.title: An opposing stance in debate
senses.titleCN: 辩论中的对立立场
senses.definition: the position of the speaker or team that argues against the motion
senses.definitionCN: 在辩论中主张反对该项动议的一方所持的立场
senses.example: The debate split into support and opposition before the first recess.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论在第一次休息前就分成了支持与反对两方。
senses.why: A debate is a physical arrangement of voices: one side proposes, the other side is placed against it.
senses.whyCN: 辩论就是声音的排布：一边提出，另一边被安置在它的对面。

senses.title: Contrast or difference
senses.titleCN: 对比与差异
senses.definition: a sharp difference between two things that are set side by side for comparison
senses.definitionCN: 两样东西并置比较时显现的鲜明差异
senses.example: The opposition between the two theories is sharper than it looks.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种理论之间的对立比表面上更尖锐。
senses.why: Two things placed opposite each other define their difference by their facing positions.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西相对摆放，正是靠面对面的位置显出彼此的差异。

senses.title: Astronomical opposition
senses.titleCN: 天体冲（行星与太阳相对）
senses.definition: the position in which a planet is on the opposite side of Earth from the sun
senses.definitionCN: 某颗行星位于地球与太阳相对一侧的位置
senses.example: Mars reaches opposition roughly every two years.
senses.exampleCN: 火星大约每两年到达一次冲的位置。
senses.why: In the sky the same geometry works: two bodies sit on opposite sides of the observer and face each other.
senses.whyCN: 天空里也是同一套几何：两个天体位于观测者的两侧，彼此相对。

senses.title: The opposing team
senses.titleCN: 体育比赛中的对手
senses.definition: the team or player that one is competing against in a match
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中与之竞争的那支队伍或那名选手
senses.example: The home side beat the opposition by three goals.
senses.exampleCN: 主队以三球击败对手。
senses.why: A match places two teams on opposite halves of the field, and the other half is simply the opposition.
senses.whyCN: 一场比赛把两支队伍放在球场的两个半场，另一半就是「对面」。

senses.title: Structural opposition
senses.titleCN: 结构上的对立
senses.definition: a relation between two elements that are defined by being different from each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个要素因彼此不同而互相界定所形成的关系
senses.example: The linguist studied the opposition between voiced and voiceless sounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这位语言学家研究浊音与清音之间的对立。
senses.why: In a system, meaning can come from position: each item is what the item opposite it is not.
senses.whyCN: 在一个系统里，意义可以来自位置：每一项就是它对那一项所不是的东西。

senses.title: A formal objection
senses.titleCN: 正式提出的反对意见
senses.definition: a written or official statement asking a court or authority to refuse something
senses.definitionCN: 请求法院或主管机关拒绝某项事项的书面或正式陈述
senses.example: The lawyers filed a formal opposition to the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们就这项合并提交了正式的反对意见。
senses.why: The physical act of standing against becomes a document that is placed against a request.
senses.whyCN: 「站到对面」这个动作变成了一份文件，被摆到某项申请的对立面。

intro.en: Opposition comes from Latin oppositio, a noun from opponere 'to place against', whose past participle is oppositus. The astronomical and political senses are later extensions of the same geometry. The exact first date in English is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语中意为「放到对面」的动词，其过去分词意为「被放到对面的」，相应的名词意为「对立、反对」。天文义与政治义都是同一套位置关系在后来的延伸。它在英语中首见的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Ponere meant 'to place, to put'. Its participle positus gave position, posit and deposit.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为「放置、安放」。它的分词形式给了「位置」「假定」「存放」等英语词。

items.en: Ob- 'against' plus ponere produced opponere 'to place in the way, to set against'. The prefix is assimilated to op- before p.
items.cn: 意为「对着」的前缀加「放置」构成这个动词，表示「挡在路上、放到对面」。前缀在唇音前同化为「欧普」的形式。

items.en: The past participle oppositus meant 'placed against, set opposite'. English opposite comes from the same participle.
items.cn: 这个过去分词意为「被放到对面的、相对的」。英语的「相反的、对面的」就出自同一分词。

items.en: The noun oppositio named the act of placing against, and later the state of being opposed.
items.cn: 相应的名词指「放到对面的动作」，后来也指「彼此相对的状态」。

items.en: Old French carried the noun toward English in the fourteenth century, still with the sense of a position facing another.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词带向英语，时间约在十四世纪，当时仍指「面对另一方的位置」。

items.en: The parliamentary sense is generally dated to the eighteenth century and the astronomical one is older in Latin; both are best described as extensions rather than separate words.
items.cn: 议会义一般认为定于十八世纪，天文义在拉丁语中更早；两者都应视为同一词的延伸，而非另立新词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin 'place against' root or a very close spelling; the second group gathers words for resisting, objecting and competing.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「放到对面」的词根，或拼写极近；第二组汇集了表示抵抗、反对与竞争的词。

entries.definition: Facing something, or completely different from it. It describes a position or a quality, not an organized campaign of resistance.
entries.definitionCN: 指面对某物，或与某物完全不同。它描述位置或性质，不指有组织的抵抗行动。

entries.definition: To argue or vote against something. It is the action; the noun names the action or the side that performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 指以言辞或投票反对某事。它是动作本身；名词则指这个动作或采取动作的一方。

entries.definition: A person who is against you in a contest or an argument. It names a rival, not the resistance as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指在竞赛或争论中与你相对的人。它指对手，不指整体的抵抗。

entries.definition: Characterized by being against something. It describes a tendency or a style, while the noun names the thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有反对特征的。它描述一种倾向或风格，而名词指事物本身。

entries.definition: The act of pushing back, often with force or endurance. It stresses holding one's ground more than stating a case.
entries.definitionCN: 指往回推的行为，常带力量或持久性。它更强调守住阵地，而不是陈述理由。

entries.definition: A reason given for disagreeing, often in a meeting or a court. It is one spoken item, not a whole side.
entries.definitionCN: 指为表示不同意而给出的理由，常出现在会议或法庭上。它是一条说出口的意见，不是一整方。

entries.definition: Disagreement with an authority or an accepted view, often on principle. It can be quiet and individual.
entries.definitionCN: 指对权威或公认看法的不认同，常出于原则。它可以是安静的、个人的。

entries.definition: A continuing contest between two sides for the same prize. It is about winning, not about blocking a proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 指两方为同一目标持续竞争。它关乎胜负，而不是阻止某项提议。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin picture of placing one thing against another, the derived family, and the fixed phrases of parliaments and matches.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：把一样东西放到另一样对面的拉丁画面、派生词族，以及议会与赛场的固定搭配。

normal.en: The prefix means 'against', the root means 'place': the whole word is a placing against.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「对着」，词根意为「放」：整个词就是「放到对面」。

normal.en: Parliament seats face each other, so the side without power is called the opposition.
normal.cn: 议会席位两两相对，所以没有权力的那一边就被称为反对方。

normal.en: A match puts two teams on opposite halves: the other half is the opposition.
normal.cn: 比赛把两队放在两个半场：另一半就是对手。

normal.en: The family runs oppose, opposite, opponent and oppositional.
normal.cn: 同族词包括反对、相反的、对手与对立的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: meet strong opposition, in opposition to, the official opposition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：遭到强烈反对、与……相对、官方反对党。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs dragged to face each other; whatever sits on one chair is defined by the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子被拖到彼此对面；坐在其中一把上的东西，由另一把来界定。

abstract.en: Opposition is not hatred; it is geometry. The other side is simply the side that faces yours.
abstract.cn: 反对不是仇恨，而是几何：另一边只是与你这一边相对的那一边。

abstract.en: The same geometry explains a debate, a lawsuit, a planet in the sky and a rival team.
abstract.cn: 同一套几何能解释一场辩论、一桩诉讼、天上的一颗行星和一支对手球队。

examples.en: Opposition to the new runway grew after the noise reports were published.
examples.cn: 噪音报告公布后，反对新建跑道的声音变大了。

examples.en: The opposition walked out when the minister refused to answer.
examples.cn: 部长拒绝回答时，反对党阵营退场了。

examples.en: In this system every sound is defined by its opposition to another sound.
examples.cn: 在这个系统里，每个音都由它与另一个音的对立来界定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧波季申」——「欧」的一边「波」到对面，另一边就「季申」申辩，正好是两方对着站

root: 拉丁 opponere「放到对面」（ob-「对着」+ ponere「放」）的过去分词 oppositus，名词 oppositio；同根词包括表示「反对」的动词、表示「对面」的形容词与表示「对手」的名词，以及同出「放置」词根的位置、组合二词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one arrangement: two things are placed face to face, and that facing becomes resistance, a rival side, a contrast, a planet in line, or a filed objection.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一种摆法出发：两样东西被放到面对面，这种相对就变成抵抗、对立的一方、差异、排成一线的一颗行星，或一份提交的异议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: place one thing against another and let each define the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一样东西放到另一样对面，让彼此互相界定。

branches.en: RESIST AND FILE: one pushes back in the street or the hearing, the other puts the refusal into an official document.
branches.cn: 抵抗与备案：一个在街头或听证会上往回推，另一个把拒绝写成正式文件。

branches.en: RIVAL SIDES: the party out of office and the team on the other half both occupy the facing position.
branches.cn: 互为对手的两方：在野阵营与另一个半场的球队，都占据着面对面的位置。

branches.en: STANCE AND DIFFERENCE: in a debate one takes a side; between two things the side becomes a visible contrast.
branches.cn: 立场与差异：在辩论中选一边；在两样东西之间，这一边就变成可见的对比。

branches.en: CELESTIAL LINE: a planet, the earth and the sun fall into the same facing arrangement.
branches.cn: 天上的连线：行星、地球与太阳排成同一套相对的位置。

branches.en: STRUCTURED PAIR: inside a system, each element is what the element opposite it is not.
branches.cn: 结构中的成对：在一个系统里，每个要素就是与它相对的那个要素所不是的东西。

intro.en: Opposition is built from a Latin prefix meaning 'against', a Latin root meaning 'place', and a Latin noun suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个意为「对着」的拉丁前缀、一个意为「放」的拉丁词根和一个拉丁名词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere 'to place' supplies the root; ob- 'against' supplies direction; -io, -ionem turns the participle into a noun of action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中意为「放」的动词提供词根；意为「对着」的前缀提供方向；名词后缀把分词变成表示动作的名词。

items.structure: ob- (Latin prefix, 'against, in the way of'; assimilated to op- before p)
items.meaningCN: 对着；迎面，语义偏移为「反对」
items.example: The prefix puts the action in someone's way.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作挡在某人路上。

items.meaningCN: 放置；安放
items.example: The root appears in compose and position.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根出现在「组成」与「位置」里。

items.meaningCN: 把自己放到对面，语义偏移为「反对、抵抗」
items.example: Several members opposed the motion.
items.exampleCN: 几名成员反对这项动议。

items.meaningCN: 被放到对面的，语义偏移为「相反的、对面的」
items.example: The bank is opposite the station.
items.exampleCN: 银行在车站对面。

items.meaning: the act or state of being against
items.meaningCN: 处于对面的动作或状态，语义偏移为「反对、反对派」
items.example: The plan met opposition at once.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划立刻遭到反对。

items.structure: op- + ponent (Latin ponens, present participle of ponere)
items.meaningCN: 把自己放到对面的人，语义偏移为「对手、反对者」
items.example: Her opponent withdrew before the final.
items.exampleCN: 她的对手在决赛前退出了。

items.meaningCN: 具有反对性质的，语义偏移为「对立的」
items.example: The party adopted an oppositional tone.
items.exampleCN: 该党采取了对抗性的语气。

items.meaningCN: 放到一起，语义偏移为「组成、创作」
items.example: Ten members compose the committee.
items.exampleCN: 十名成员组成这个委员会。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 放到对面；被放到对面的

definition_zh: 在野党；反对党；与执政方相对的政党
definition_en: the political party, or the largest party, that is not in government and opposes the governing side
core_image: 议会大厅里，执政者坐在一边，另一边的人站起来逐条挑错，桌上摆着另一份预算
scene: 议事厅里两排长椅相对，一份预算刚发下，另一排人立刻翻到附录逐行质疑。The opposition party demanded a full debate on the budget.
sceneCN: 议事厅里两排长椅相对，一份预算刚发下，另一排人立刻翻到附录逐行质疑；句中的这个说法指「不在政府内、以反对执政方为职责的政党」（第 1 个义项：选举后未掌权、在议会中与政府相对的那一个政党）。图中可辨识物件：两排长椅、预算册、附录页、麦克风、记者的笔记本。

pos.zh: 在野党；反对党（可数）
（作定语）在野党的；反对党的

senses.title: The party out of office
senses.titleCN: 不在政府内的政党
senses.definition: the party that lost or did not enter government and now sits outside the executive
senses.definitionCN: 未能执政或未进入政府、如今置身行政机构之外的政党
senses.example: The opposition party has promised to reverse the cuts.
senses.exampleCN: 在野党承诺要撤销这些削减。
senses.why: Parliament is arranged as two facing benches: whoever does not sit on the government bench sits opposite it.
senses.whyCN: 议会排成两排相对的座椅：不坐政府那一排的人，就坐在它的对面。

senses.title: The official or largest opposition
senses.titleCN: 官方反对党或最大反对党
senses.definition: the opposition party formally recognized as the main alternative, with special rights and funding
senses.definitionCN: 被正式认定为主要替代选项的反对党，享有特定权利与经费
senses.example: The official opposition party receives a state allowance for research.
senses.exampleCN: 官方反对党获得国家拨付的研究经费。
senses.why: A chamber needs one recognizable voice to answer the government, so the largest opposing group is given that role.
senses.whyCN: 议事机构需要一个可辨认的声音来回应政府，于是最大的反对团体被赋予这一角色。

senses.title: The mirror in a two-party system
senses.titleCN: 两党制下的在野党
senses.definition: in a system with two dominant parties, the one currently outside office
senses.definitionCN: 在两强主导的制度中，当下不掌权的那一个政党
senses.example: In a two-party system the opposition party is simply the other half of the seesaw.
senses.exampleCN: 在两党制下，在野党不过是跷跷板的另一半。
senses.why: With only two large options, the opposition is not a small critic but the government-in-waiting.
senses.whyCN: 只有两个大选项时，在野党不是小小的批评者，而是候任政府。

senses.title: The shadow cabinet role
senses.titleCN: 影子内阁角色
senses.definition: the group of opposition politicians who mirror each minister and prepare alternative policies
senses.definitionCN: 由在野政治人物组成、一一对应各部并准备替代政策的一组人
senses.example: Each opposition party spokesperson is paired with a minister.
senses.exampleCN: 反对党每位发言人都与一位部长对应。
senses.why: To be ready to govern, the party out of office builds a duplicate cabinet that watches each department.
senses.whyCN: 为了随时能够执政，在野党会搭一个复制版内阁，逐个盯住各部。

senses.title: A party built to challenge
senses.titleCN: 为挑战执政党而组建的党
senses.definition: a party founded mainly to displace the governing side rather than to defend an old interest
senses.definitionCN: 主要为了取代执政方、而非维护旧有利益而成立的政党
senses.example: The new opposition party was founded by mayors from three regions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新的反对党由三个地区的市长创立。
senses.why: Some parties begin as movements against a government; their first programme is often simply 'not them'.
senses.whyCN: 有些政党起初就是反对现政府的运动，其第一份纲领往往只是「不要他们」。

senses.title: Opposition on a local council
senses.titleCN: 地方议会在野党
senses.definition: the group on a town or city council that opposes the local administration
senses.definitionCN: 在镇议会或市议会中与地方行政当局相对的团体
senses.example: The local opposition party forced a review of the bus routes.
senses.exampleCN: 地方在野党促成了对公交线路的复核。
senses.why: The same facing benches appear in miniature wherever a council meets.
senses.whyCN: 只要议事机构开会，同样的一对座椅就会以缩小的形式出现。

senses.title: An opposition alliance
senses.titleCN: 在野党联盟
senses.definition: several opposition parties acting together to challenge one government
senses.definitionCN: 若干个在野政党共同行动、挑战同一个政府
senses.example: Four opposition parties formed an alliance before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 四个反对党在投票前结成了联盟。
senses.why: When one party is too small to face the government alone, several opposing parties line up on the same bench.
senses.whyCN: 当一个政党太小、无法独自面对政府时，几个反对党就排到同一条长椅上。

senses.title: The scrutiny function
senses.titleCN: 监督与问责职能
senses.definition: the job of questioning ministers, demanding documents and publicizing failures
senses.definitionCN: 质询部长、索取文件并把失误公之于众的职责
senses.example: The opposition party used its committee seats to request the reports.
senses.exampleCN: 反对党利用它在委员会的席位索要那些报告。
senses.why: A party without power still holds a function: it keeps the government's answers on the record.
senses.whyCN: 没有权力的政党仍有一项职能：把政府的回答留在记录里。

intro.en: The phrase joins opposition, from Latin opponere 'to place against', with party, from Latin pars 'part'. English speakers combined them as parliamentary benches took their modern shape; the first use is not securely dated.
intro.cn: 这个说法把出自拉丁语「放到对面」的名词，与出自拉丁语「部分」的名词拼在一起。英语使用者把两者组合起来，大约与议会两排座椅形成现代格局同时；首次使用的时间不能确证。

items.en: Ob- 'against' plus ponere 'place' produced opponere 'to set against'. Its participle oppositus gave opposition.
items.cn: 意为「对着」的前缀加「放」构成表示「放到对面」的动词，其分词形式后来给出「反对」这一名词。

items.en: Pars, partis meant 'part, share'. Through Old French it gave English party, first a part or a side.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词意为「部分、份」，经古法语给出英语中表示「一部分」或「一方」的名词。

items.en: Old French opposition and partie carried both halves toward English, where they were later joined in one phrase.
items.cn: 古法语中表示「反对」与「部分」的两个词分别把两半带进英语，后来才被拼进同一个短语。

items.en: From the eighteenth century, writers began to speak of the party in opposition, meaning the side facing the ministers. The exact first use of the full phrase is uncertain.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，作者们开始说「处于反对地位的政党」，指面对部长们的那一方。完整短语的首见时间不确定。

items.en: As disciplined parties and mass electorates grew, the label became a fixed parliamentary term, with an official leader and a shadow team.
items.cn: 随着纪律严明的政党与大规模选民出现，这个说法成为固定的议会术语，并配有正式领袖与影子团队。

items.en: The phrase now travels beyond Westminster and describes any party outside government, from a city council to a national assembly.
items.cn: 如今这个说法已走出英国议会，可指任何不掌权的政党，从市议会到国民议会皆可。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two halves or a very close form; the second group names the other seats and alliances around a government.
note.cn: 第一组共享两个组成部分之一，或形式极近；第二组指政府周围的其他席位与联盟。

entries.definition: The act of resisting or the whole side that opposes. It can name a camp without naming a single organized party.
entries.definitionCN: 指抵抗的行为或整个反对阵营。它可以指一个阵营，却不必指某一个有组织的政党。

entries.definition: The one-word noun is far broader: a gathering, a legal side or any political group. The phrase adds the specific role.
entries.definitionCN: 单用的名词宽得多：聚会、法律上的一方或任何政治团体；加上前面的修饰后才指出具体角色。

entries.definition: A loyal supporter of a side, often one who will not listen to the other. It never names the institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一方的忠实支持者，往往不听另一方的话。它从不指制度本身。

entries.definition: The adjective for the side that argues against. It can describe a team or a lawyer, not only a parliamentary group.
entries.definitionCN: 指持反对立场的那一方的形容词，可形容球队或律师，不限于议会团体。

entries.definition: The party that holds office and answers for the government. It is the exact opposite seat to the phrase in question.
entries.definitionCN: 指掌握职位、为政府作答的政党，正好是本条所指席位的对面。

entries.definition: A party with fewer seats than the largest one. It may be an opposition party or merely a small partner in a coalition.
entries.definitionCN: 指席位少于最大党的政党。它可能是在野党，也可能只是联盟中的小伙伴。

entries.definition: A deal among several parties to act together. An opposition party is one organization; a coalition may contain several.
entries.definitionCN: 指若干政党共同行动的协议。在野党是一个组织，联盟则可能包含好几个。

entries.definition: A person or group competing for the same prize. It stresses competition, while the phrase stresses institutional position.
entries.definitionCN: 指为同一目标竞争的人或团体。它强调竞争，而本条短语强调制度位置。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real components, the parliamentary picture of facing benches, real derived words and fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的构件、议会里两排相对座椅的画面、真实派生词与固定搭配。

normal.en: The first half means 'placed against'; the second half means 'part'. Together: the part placed against the government.
normal.cn: 前半段意为「放到对面」，后半段意为「部分」；合起来就是「被放到政府对面的那部分人」。

normal.en: The official opposition is the largest opposing group, and it receives money and staff for the role.
normal.cn: 官方反对党就是最大的反对团体，并因此获得经费与人员。

normal.en: Its mirror is the party that holds office, sitting on the other bench.
normal.cn: 它的镜像就是掌握职位、坐在另一条长椅上的政党。

normal.en: The family runs opposition, oppositional, oppose, opponent and partisan.
normal.cn: 同族词包括反对、对立的、反对、对手与党派支持者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the role: the official opposition party, the largest opposition party, an opposition spokesperson.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出角色：官方反对党、最大在野党、反对党发言人。

abstract.en: Picture two benches facing each other across a narrow aisle; the empty one is not empty for long.
abstract.cn: 想象两条长椅隔着窄窄的过道相对；空着的那条不会空太久。

abstract.en: The party out of office is a government folded up and stored, waiting for the next election to unfold it.
abstract.cn: 在野党就是被折叠收起的政府，等下一次选举把它展开。

abstract.en: Its daily work is not to win but to keep the other bench answering out loud.
abstract.cn: 它每天的工作不是取胜，而是让对面那条长椅大声作答。

examples.en: The opposition party tabled an alternative budget within an hour of the speech.
examples.cn: 反对党在演讲结束后一小时内提交了一份替代预算。

examples.en: An opposition party with only twelve seats can still force a recorded vote.
examples.cn: 只有十二个席位的在野党仍能迫使进行记名投票。

examples.en: The opposition party's shadow team met the teachers' union before the review.
examples.cn: 反对党的影子团队在复核前会见了教师工会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧波季申·帕提」——先「欧」到对面「波」一下，再「季申」自己的方案，最后带上自己的那一「派」，正是对着政府的在野党

root: 前半出自拉丁 opponere「放到对面」（ob-「对着」+ ponere「放」）的分词 oppositus 与名词 oppositio；后半经古法语上溯到拉丁 pars/partem「部分、份」。合起来即「被放到政府对面的那部分人」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the same bench: a party out of office, sometimes officially recognized, sometimes one half of a two-party mirror, and always carrying a shadow team and a duty to scrutinize.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一条长椅展开：不掌权的政党，有时被正式认定，有时是两党镜像的另一半，并且始终带着影子团队与监督职责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the bench that faces the government and keeps it answering.
core.cn: 核心意象：面向政府、逼它作答的那条长椅。

branches.en: OUT AND CHALLENGING: one simply sits outside office; the other was founded to push the governing side aside.
branches.cn: 在外与来挑战：一个只是坐在政府之外，另一个从成立起就是要挤走执政方。

branches.en: RECOGNIZED MIRROR: the largest opposing group gets formal rights, and in a two-party system the mirror is the whole alternative.
branches.cn: 被承认的镜像：最大的反对团体获得正式权利；在两党制下，这面镜子就是全部的替代选项。

branches.en: SHADOW AND SCRUTINY: a duplicate cabinet prepares policy while the same members demand documents and answers.
branches.cn: 影子与监督：一套复制内阁准备政策，同一批成员则索要文件与答复。

branches.en: LOCAL SCALE: the same facing benches appear in a town hall, with the same function in miniature.
branches.cn: 地方尺度：同样的相对座椅出现在市政厅，职能只是缩小了。

branches.en: JOINED BENCH: several opposing parties may line up together when none is strong enough alone.
branches.cn: 合并的长椅：当没有一个足够强大时，几个反对党可以排到一起。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two Latin roots, one meaning 'place against' and one meaning 'part', each with its own English family.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁词根构成，一个意为「放到对面」，一个意为「部分」，各自都带一串英语同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin opponere supplies the first element through its participle and noun; Latin pars, partem supplies the second through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中意为「放到对面」的动词经其分词与名词提供第一段；拉丁语中意为「部分」的名词经古法语提供第二段。

items.meaningCN: 处于对面的状态，语义偏移为「反对、反对阵营」
items.example: The motion passed despite opposition.
items.exampleCN: 这项动议虽有反对仍然通过。

items.meaningCN: 具有反对性质的，语义偏移为「对立的」
items.example: The group took an oppositional stance.
items.exampleCN: 该团体采取了对立姿态。

items.meaningCN: 把自己放到对面，语义偏移为「反对」
items.example: Two ministers opposed the bill.
items.exampleCN: 两位部长反对这项法案。

items.meaningCN: 被放到对面的，语义偏移为「相反的、对面的」
items.example: The office is opposite the library.
items.exampleCN: 办公室在图书馆对面。

items.meaningCN: 被放到对面的人，语义偏移为「对手」
items.example: His opponent spoke first.
items.exampleCN: 他的对手先发言。

items.structure: part- (Latin pars, partem 'part') + -y (noun suffix through Old French -ie)
items.meaningCN: 部分或一方，语义偏移为「政党」
items.example: The party held its conference in June.
items.exampleCN: 该党在六月举行大会。

items.structure: part- + -isan (adherent suffix via French and Italian)
items.meaningCN: 某一方的跟随者，语义偏移为「党徒、偏袒的」
items.example: Partisan attacks dominated the debate.
items.exampleCN: 党派攻击主导了辩论。

items.meaningCN: 由两方共同支持的，语义偏移为「跨党派的」
items.example: The bill won bipartisan support.
items.exampleCN: 这项法案赢得跨党派支持。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 放到对面；被放到对面的

definition_zh: 联盟；联合政府；合并；军事联盟；商业联盟；临时性结合
definition_en: a temporary alliance of parties, groups or states formed to act together for a shared purpose
core_image: 几张桌子拼成一张长桌，各家的名牌并排摆着，散会时又各自搬回原处
scene: 选后第二天，几间办公室的门牌还挂着各自的名称，桌上却已摊开同一份组阁名单。The two smaller groups formed a coalition after the election.
sceneCN: 选后第二天，几间办公室的门牌还挂着各自的名称，桌上却已摊开同一份组阁名单；句中的这个词指「若干团体为共同目的结成的联盟」（第 1 个义项：政党之间为组成政府或共同行动而订立的合作安排）。图中可辨识物件：拼起的长桌、各家名牌、组阁名单、铅笔、门口的名牌。

pos.zh: 联盟；联合政府；合并体（可数）
（作定语）联盟的；联合的

senses.title: An alliance of parties
senses.titleCN: 政党之间的联盟
senses.definition: an arrangement in which two or more parties agree to act together, often to command a majority
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个政党约定共同行动、常为取得多数席位的安排
senses.example: The two parties signed a coalition after weeks of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 两党经过数周谈判后签署了联盟协议。
senses.why: Separate groups grow together for one purpose: each keeps its own name while acting as one body.
senses.whyCN: 各自独立的团体为同一个目的长到一起：各自保留名号，却作为一个整体行动。

senses.title: A coalition government
senses.titleCN: 联合政府
senses.definition: a government formed by more than one party sharing ministries and responsibility
senses.definitionCN: 由不止一个政党共同组成、分享各部职位与责任的政府
senses.example: The coalition government lasted only eighteen months.
senses.exampleCN: 这个联合政府只维持了十八个月。
senses.why: When no party wins a majority, the alliance itself must take on the shape of a government.
senses.whyCN: 当没有一个政党赢得多数时，联盟本身就必须长成政府的形状。

senses.title: An alliance of states or bodies
senses.titleCN: 国家或组织之间的联盟
senses.definition: a group of states, unions or organizations that agree to cooperate on a common aim
senses.definitionCN: 就共同目标约定合作的一群国家、团体或组织
senses.example: A coalition of coastal cities lobbied for cleaner shipping fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 一群沿海城市游说推行更清洁的船用燃料。
senses.why: The same logic works above the level of parties: separate members join for a shared aim.
senses.whyCN: 同一套逻辑在政党之上也成立：各自独立的成员为共同目标联合。

senses.title: The act of merging
senses.titleCN: 合并的动作
senses.definition: the process by which separate parts grow or come together into one mass
senses.definitionCN: 各自分离的部分长合或聚成一个整体的过程
senses.example: The coalition of the two firms took effect in April.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司的合并于四月生效。
senses.why: The word first names a physical growing together; the political alliance is that process applied to groups.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指物理上的长合；政治联盟就是把这一过程用在团体上。

senses.title: A military coalition
senses.titleCN: 军事联盟
senses.definition: a group of armed forces from several countries fighting or training together
senses.definitionCN: 由若干国家的武装力量共同作战或共同训练形成的集团
senses.example: The military coalition flew joint patrols over the region.
senses.exampleCN: 军事联盟在该地区上空进行联合巡逻。
senses.why: Armies from separate states join under one command, keeping their own flags but sharing a plan.
senses.whyCN: 不同国家的军队归入同一指挥之下，各自保留旗帜，却共用一份计划。

senses.title: An advocacy or business alliance
senses.titleCN: 倡议或商业联盟
senses.definition: a loose alliance of companies or campaigners formed to press one common demand
senses.definitionCN: 由公司或倡议者组成的松散联盟，为提出同一项诉求而行动
senses.example: A coalition of retailers asked for a delay in the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 一群零售商组成的联盟要求推迟新规。
senses.why: Any group too small to be heard alone can grow together with others and speak once.
senses.whyCN: 任何独自发声太小的团体，都可以与别人长到一起，只发一次声。

senses.title: A temporary combination
senses.titleCN: 临时性结合
senses.definition: a union made for a limited task or period, expected to dissolve afterwards
senses.definitionCN: 为有限的任务或时段结成、预期事后会解散的联合
senses.example: Their coalition was temporary and ended with the single vote.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的联盟是临时的，随着那一次投票结束而终止。
senses.why: Growing together does not mean fusing for ever: the parts can separate once the shared aim is met.
senses.whyCN: 长到一起不等于永久融合：共同目标一旦达成，各部分仍可分开。

senses.title: Coalition politics as a practice
senses.titleCN: 联盟政治的实践
senses.definition: the everyday work of negotiating, sharing posts and holding an alliance together
senses.definitionCN: 谈判、分配职位并把联盟维系下去的日常工作
senses.example: Coalition politics rewards patience more than rhetoric.
senses.exampleCN: 联盟政治奖赏耐心，而不是辞令。
senses.why: Once an alliance exists, it becomes a practice: meetings, quotas and compromises rather than a single signature.
senses.whyCN: 联盟一旦存在，就变成一种实践：会议、配额与妥协，而不是一次签字。

intro.en: Coalition comes from Latin coalescere 'to grow together', built from co- 'together' and alescere 'to grow'. The political sense is a later English extension. The word's first appearance in English is not securely dated.
intro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语中意为「长到一起」的动词，由意为「共同」的前缀与意为「生长」的词根构成。政治义是英语里后来的延伸。它在英语中首见的时间不能确证。

items.en: Alescere was an inceptive verb meaning 'to begin to grow'. It is related to alere 'to nourish' and to adultus 'grown up'.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词是表示「开始生长」的起始动词，与意为「滋养」的动词及意为「已长成的」分词同族。

items.en: Co- 'together' plus alescere gave coalescere 'to grow together, to unite into one body'. The image is biological, not political.
items.cn: 意为「共同」的前缀加「生长」构成表示「长到一起、并成一个整体」的动词。这个画面是生物性的，不是政治的。

items.en: The past participle coalitus meant 'grown together'. From its stem the noun coalitio was formed.
items.cn: 过去分词意为「已经长到一起的」。名词形式正是从这个词干构成的。

items.en: French took the Latin noun as coalition and used it for a union of parties or groups. English borrowed the French form rather than the Latin one.
items.cn: 法语借入这个拉丁名词，用来指政党或团体的联合。英语借的是法语形式，而不是拉丁形式。

items.en: In English the word settled into political life during the eighteenth century, when ministries began to be built from several factions. The exact first use remains uncertain.
items.cn: 在英语里，这个词于十八世纪进入政治生活，当时内阁开始由若干派系拼组。确切的首见时间仍不确定。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word spread to military, business and campaign alliances, always keeping the idea of separate parts acting as one.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词扩展到军事、商业与倡议联盟，始终保留「各自独立的部分作为一个整体行动」的意思。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root of growing together; the second group gathers words for alliances of different strength and duration.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「长到一起」的词根；第二组汇集了强度与持续时间各不相同的联盟说法。

entries.definition: To grow together into one body. It names the process; the noun names the resulting alliance.
entries.definitionCN: 指长合成为一个整体。它指过程，名词则指长合之后形成的联盟。

entries.definition: The process of merging, often physical or chemical. It does not by itself mean a political deal.
entries.definitionCN: 指合并的过程，常是物理或化学过程。它本身不指政治交易。

entries.definition: In the process of growing together. It describes the state, not the finished group.
entries.definitionCN: 指正处于长合过程中的。它描述状态，而不是已经成形的团体。

entries.definition: Of or belonging to a coalition. It is the adjective built on the noun, not a separate alliance.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于联盟的。它是从名词构成的形容词，不是另一种联盟。

entries.definition: A union of groups or states, often sealed by a treaty and meant to last. A coalition is usually narrower and more temporary.
entries.definitionCN: 指团体或国家的联合，常以条约缔结、意在持久。联盟通常更窄，也更临时。

entries.definition: An association of states, clubs or people for a common cause. It often has a name and a membership list.
entries.definitionCN: 指为国家、俱乐部或人因共同事业结成的协会，常有名称与成员名单。

entries.definition: A group of states or members that votes as one. It stresses weight in a vote rather than a written deal.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为一个单位投票的一群国家或成员。它强调投票分量，而不是书面协议。

entries.definition: A joining of parts into one body, often permanent and sometimes losing separate identities.
entries.definitionCN: 指把各部分并成一个整体，常为永久，有时会失去各自的独立身份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin picture of growing together, the derived family, and the fixed phrases of government and war.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语「长到一起」的画面、派生词族，以及政府与战争语境中的固定搭配。

normal.en: The prefix means 'together', the root means 'grow': the whole word is a growing together.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「共同」，词根意为「生长」：整个词就是「长到一起」。

normal.en: Separate parties keep their own names while growing into one government.
normal.cn: 各自独立的政党保留自己的名号，却长成一个政府。

normal.en: The family runs coalesce, coalescence, coalescent and coalitional.
normal.cn: 同族词包括合并、合并过程、合并中的与联盟的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: form a coalition, a coalition government, a military coalition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：组成联盟、联合政府、军事联盟。

normal.en: Its weakness is built in: a coalition can break up as easily as it was formed.
normal.cn: 它的弱点写在构造里：联盟解散可以和组成一样容易。

abstract.en: Picture several pots of paint poured into one can: the colours touch but do not mix at once.
abstract.cn: 想象几罐颜料倒进同一个桶：颜色挨在一起，却没有立刻混匀。

abstract.en: A coalition is a shared table, not a shared identity; each name card stays on the table.
abstract.cn: 联盟是一张共用的桌子，而不是共用的身份；每张名牌始终摆在桌上。

abstract.en: It ends when the common purpose ends, which is why it is strong today and fragile tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 共同目标结束，它也就结束；所以它今天坚固，明天脆弱。

examples.en: Without a majority, the largest party had to build a coalition within a week.
examples.cn: 由于没有多数，最大党必须在一周内搭起一个联盟。

examples.en: The coalition broke apart over a single clause in the budget.
examples.cn: 这个联盟因为预算里的一条条款而瓦解。

examples.en: A coalition of universities shared the cost of the telescope.
examples.cn: 一个大学联盟分担了这台望远镜的费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扣阿利申」——把几股人「扣」在一起，讲「阿」字顺，只有「利」害一致才「申」明组阁，正好是一个联盟

root: 拉丁 coalescere「长到一起」= co-（共同）+ alescere「生长」，过去分词 coalitus，名词 coalitio；同根词包括表示「合并」的动词、表示「合并过程」的名词与表示「正在合并」的形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all come from one biological picture: separate parts grow together, then keep separate names while acting as a single body for as long as the purpose lasts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都出自同一个生物画面：各自分离的部分长到一起，随后保留各自的名号，只要目的还在，就作为一个整体行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate parts grow together, share a purpose, and can still come apart.
core.cn: 核心意象：各自独立的部分长到一起，共用一个目的，也仍可能重新分开。

branches.en: DEAL AND GOVERNMENT: first the parties agree, then that agreement puts on the shape of a cabinet.
branches.cn: 协议与政府：先是政党达成协议，随后这份协议长成内阁的形状。

branches.en: STATES AND ARMIES: the same union works among cities and among armed forces under one command.
branches.cn: 国家与军队：同一套联合也用于城市之间，以及归入同一指挥的武装力量之间。

branches.en: MERGE AND DISSOLVE: the act of growing together and the limited term that lets the parts separate again.
branches.cn: 合并与解散：长合的动作，以及允许各部分重新分开的有限期限。

branches.en: SMALL VOICES JOINED: shops or campaigners too quiet alone grow together and speak once.
branches.cn: 微弱的声音合起来：独自太轻的商家或倡议者长到一起，只发一次声。

branches.en: DAILY PRACTICE: keeping the alliance alive takes meetings, quotas and compromise, not one signature.
branches.cn: 日常实践：维系联盟靠会议、配额与妥协，而不是一次签字。

intro.en: Coalition is built from a Latin prefix, a Latin root and a Latin noun suffix, and the same pieces build a compact family.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁词根和一个拉丁名词后缀构成，同样的构件还构成一个紧凑的词族。

latinIntro.en: Co- 'together' supplies the prefix; alescere 'to grow' supplies the root; -itio, -itionem turns the participle into a noun of action.
latinIntro.cn: 意为「共同」的前缀提供第一段；意为「生长」的词根提供第二段；名词后缀把分词变成表示动作的名词。

items.structure: co- (Latin prefix, 'together, with'; variant con- before some consonants)
items.meaningCN: 共同；一起，语义偏移为「联合」
items.example: The prefix marks joint action in many verbs.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀在许多动词里标出共同行动。

items.meaningCN: 生长；长成
items.example: The root is visible in adult and adolescent.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根在「成年」与「青春期的」里仍可看出。

items.meaningCN: 长合在一起，语义偏移为「合并、联合」
items.example: The two streams coalesce below the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 两条溪流在桥下汇合。

items.structure: coalesce + -ence (noun suffix of state or process)
items.meaningCN: 长合的过程，语义偏移为「融合、合并」
items.example: Coalescence of the droplets formed a single drop.
items.exampleCN: 小滴融合成了一个单滴。

items.meaningCN: 正在长合的，语义偏移为「合并中的」
items.example: The coalescent groups soon spoke with one voice.
items.exampleCN: 这些正在合并的团体很快用同一个声音说话。

items.structure: co- + alit- (from Latin coalitus 'grown together') + -ion (Latin noun suffix)
items.meaningCN: 长到一起的团体，语义偏移为「联盟、联合政府」
items.example: The coalition held its first meeting on Friday.
items.exampleCN: 该联盟在周五举行了第一次会议。

items.meaning: of or belonging to a coalition
items.meaningCN: 属于联盟的，语义偏移为「联盟的、联合的」
items.example: Coalitional discipline held for six months.
items.exampleCN: 联盟纪律维持了六个月。

items.meaning: in the act of growing together
items.meaningCN: 正在进行长合的，语义偏移为「合并中的」
items.example: The coalescing factions chose one chairman.
items.exampleCN: 正在合并的各派选出了一位主席。

latinEntries.structure: past participle of coalescere, stem coalit-

definition_zh: 联合政府；多党联合内阁；联合执政的一届任期；多数联合政府；少数联合政府；大联合政府；看守联合政府；地方联合执政
definition_en: a government formed by two or more parties that agree on a shared programme and divide the cabinet posts between them
core_image: 两排原本各站一边的人把旗子并到同一张长桌后，在一份分工名单上共同落笔
scene: 大选得票分散，没有任何党派拿到过半席位，参政党派的谈判代表隔着长桌逐条核对部长职位，最后把共同纲领摊在桌面中央。A coalition government was sworn in after no party won a majority.
sceneCN: 大选后各党得票分散，参政党派的代表隔着长桌核对部长职位，最后把共同纲领摊在桌面中央；句中的短语指「由多个政党协议共组的内阁」（第 1 个义项：两个以上政党签约共同执政、按协议分配部长席位）。图中可辨识物件：长桌、部长职位清单、共同纲领、并排的党旗、宣誓用的文件夹。

pos.zh: 联合政府；多党联合内阁（可数短语）
联合执政的时期；一届联合任期
作定语，指联合政府的（纲领、政策、纪律）

collocations.phrase: a coalition government led by the largest party
collocations.zh: 由最大党主导的联合政府

derivatives.zh: 联合；联盟（短语的核心名词）
主张多党联合执政的人

senses.title: Parties agree to govern as one
senses.titleCN: 两个以上政党签约共同执政
senses.definition: the cabinet that results when two or more parties sign a common programme and divide the ministerial posts between them
senses.definitionCN: 两个以上政党签署共同纲领、分配部长职位之后形成的内阁
senses.example: After weeks of bargaining, the two parties announced a coalition government.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数周讨价还价，两党宣布组成联合政府。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'grow together': separate parties, like separate shoots, fuse into one body at the negotiating table.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「长到一起」：原本分开的政党像分开的枝条，在谈判桌边合成一个整体。

senses.title: The cabinet as a working body
senses.titleCN: 作为运转班子的联合内阁本身
senses.definition: the group of ministers drawn from the partner parties, considered as one body with its own meetings, papers and staff
senses.definitionCN: 由各伙伴党派抽调部长组成的班子，作为有会议、文件与班底的单一机构来看待
senses.example: The coalition government held its first cabinet meeting on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 联合内阁在周一召开了第一次内阁会议。
senses.why: Once the bargain is signed, the arrangement turns into an institution: the phrase stops naming the deal and starts naming the people who meet each week.
senses.whyCN: 协议签署之后，这个安排就变成机构：此时这个短语不再指那笔交易，而指每周开会的那批人。

senses.title: The term served under such a cabinet
senses.titleCN: 联合执政的一届任期
senses.definition: the stretch of time from the swearing-in to the break-up during which the partners govern together
senses.definitionCN: 从宣誓就职到合作破裂之间、各党共同执政的那段时间
senses.example: That coalition government survived only fourteen months.
senses.exampleCN: 那一届联合政府只维持了十四个月。
senses.why: A cabinet is an event with a beginning and an end, so the same phrase can name the whole span rather than the body.
senses.whyCN: 一届内阁是有始有终的事件，因此同一个短语也能指整段时间，而不只是那个班子。

senses.title: A partnership with a majority
senses.titleCN: 席位过半、无需外援即可立法的联合政府
senses.definition: a partnership whose combined seats pass half the chamber, so it can legislate without help from outside parties
senses.definitionCN: 各党席位相加超过议会半数，无需外部政党支持即可立法的联合政府
senses.example: The two centre parties had enough seats for a majority coalition government.
senses.exampleCN: 两个中间派政党的席位足以组成多数联合政府。
senses.why: Seat arithmetic decides how strong the fusion is: a majority turns the partnership into a self-sufficient machine.
senses.whyCN: 席位算术决定这种合并有多结实：席位过半就把伙伴关系变成一台自足的机器。

senses.title: A partnership living on outside votes
senses.titleCN: 未过半、靠外部支持维持的少数联合政府
senses.definition: a partnership that holds office without half the seats, relying on the votes of parties outside the cabinet
senses.definitionCN: 席位不到半数、依靠内阁之外政党的投票维持执政的联合政府
senses.example: A minority coalition government must negotiate every budget with independents.
senses.exampleCN: 少数联合政府每份预算都得与独立议员协商。
senses.why: Growing together without a majority leaves the seam visible: every bill tests whether the partners can still hold hands.
senses.whyCN: 没有过半就合到一起，接缝始终露在外面：每一份法案都在检验伙伴们还能不能继续牵手。

senses.title: A grand bargain between the big rivals
senses.titleCN: 两大对手政党合组的大联合政府
senses.definition: an arrangement in which the two largest rival parties, normally opponents, share the cabinet during a crisis
senses.definitionCN: 通常在危机时期由两个最大的对立政党分享内阁的安排
senses.example: A grand coalition government was the only way out of the deadlock.
senses.exampleCN: 大联合政府是走出僵局的唯一办法。
senses.why: The fusion is most surprising when the partners were enemies: the phrase keeps its literal force, two things made one.
senses.whyCN: 当伙伴原本是敌人时，这种合并最出人意料：这个短语仍保留字面力量——两样东西变成一样。

senses.title: A stopgap cabinet
senses.titleCN: 看守或过渡性的联合政府
senses.definition: a temporary partnership that keeps the state running until a fresh election or a lasting agreement
senses.definitionCN: 在新选举或持久协议达成之前维持国家运转的临时联合班子
senses.example: A caretaker coalition government supervised the ballot and then resigned.
senses.exampleCN: 看守联合政府主持了投票，随后辞职。
senses.why: If the parties cannot yet agree on a full term, they can still agree on a short one: fusion with an expiry date.
senses.whyCN: 如果各党暂时无法就完整任期达成一致，仍可就一个短任期达成一致：带到期日的合并。

senses.title: The same device at local level
senses.titleCN: 地方与地区层面的联合执政
senses.definition: the same arrangement in a city, region or devolved assembly, often used to keep a single rival party out of office
senses.definitionCN: 在市、地区或下放权力的议会中采用的同一安排，常用来把某个对手政党挡在执政位置之外
senses.example: At city hall a coalition government of two small groups replaced the long-ruling party.
senses.exampleCN: 在市政厅，两个小党派的联合政府取代了长期执政的党。
senses.why: The pattern is scale-free: wherever seats are counted and posts are divided, partners can grow together.
senses.whyCN: 这种模式不分尺度：只要席位需要清点、职位需要分配，伙伴们就能合到一起。

intro.en: The word starts in Latin as an image of things growing into one another. Its use for a cabinet is a modern political extension rather than part of the original meaning, and coalition ministries were already called by that name in the late eighteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词在拉丁语里最初是「事物彼此长合」的画面。用它指内阁属于近代的政治延伸，并非原义；十八世纪晚期的联合内阁已被这样称呼。

items.en: Alere 'to nourish, to feed' gave alescere, a verb meaning to begin to grow; the same family lies behind adolescent and adult.
items.cn: 意为「滋养、喂养」的拉丁动词衍生出「开始生长」的动词；「青少年」与「成年人」这两个英语词也出自同一族。

items.en: Co- 'together' plus alescere 'begin to grow' made coalescere 'to grow together, to fuse'; its past participle coalitus is the base of the noun of union.
items.cn: 表示「共同」的前缀加「开始生长」，构成「长到一起、合而为一」的拉丁动词；其过去分词是「联合」这一名词的基础。

items.en: The noun coalitio, built on that participle, named a growing together or a league; English took the political sense through French coalition, where it had meant a league of powers.
items.cn: 由该分词构成的拉丁名词指「长合」或「同盟」；英语经法语借入这一政治用法，法语中它曾指列强之间的同盟。

items.en: In seventeenth and eighteenth century French, coalition meant a temporary league of states or parties formed against a common rival.
items.cn: 在十七、十八世纪的法语里，这个词指国家或党派为对付共同对手而结成的临时同盟。

items.en: British politics applied it to cabinets: the Fox-North ministry of 1783 was widely called a coalition, and the label stuck to any multi-party cabinet.
items.cn: 英国政治把它用到内阁上：一七八三年的福克斯与诺斯联合内阁被普遍称作联合政府，此后任何多党内阁都沿用这一称呼。

items.en: In the twentieth century the phrase widened to cover majority and minority coalitions, grand coalitions of rivals, caretaker cabinets and coalitions in devolved assemblies.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个短语扩展到涵盖多数与少数联合政府、由对手组成的大联合政府、看守内阁，以及下放权力议会中的联合执政。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds close to the headword, and only one of them shares its root; the second group names neighbouring arrangements that are not the same thing.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或读音上与词条接近，其中只有一个与它同源；第二组是相邻但不等同的制度安排。

entries.definition: The noun for any union of groups; on its own it can be a campaign alliance, an electoral pact or a business bloc, with no cabinet involved.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何团体结成的联合体；单独使用时可以指竞选同盟、选举协议或商业联盟，并不涉及内阁。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun comes: separate parts merge into one mass, as cells or ideas do. It never means to form a cabinet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词所由来的动词：分开的部分合并成一团，如细胞或想法；它从不表示组阁。

entries.definition: The process of merging, used in physics and linguistics; it names the fusing, not the resulting body.
entries.definitionCN: 合并的过程，用于物理学与语言学；它指合并本身，而非合并后的机构。

entries.definition: From a Latin verb meaning 'to bring together', but it means comparing texts or gathering pages, not a political union.
entries.definitionCN: 出自意为「带到一起」的拉丁动词，但指比对文本或整理书页，与政治联合无关。

entries.definition: A general agreement to work together, often between states or parties and often for one purpose only; it need not produce a cabinet.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指合作约定，常见于国家或政党之间，往往只为一件事，不必产生内阁。

entries.definition: The name used when most parties join a cabinet to face a war, a collapse or a transition; the emphasis is on ending division, not on seat arithmetic.
entries.definitionCN: 多数党派为应对战争、崩溃或过渡而加入内阁时用的名称；强调结束分裂，而非席位数。

entries.definition: A cabinet formed by a single party that lacks a majority and governs with outside support; only one party holds the posts.
entries.definitionCN: 由单一政党组成、席位不过半、靠外部支持执政的内阁；部长职位只由一个党占有。

entries.definition: A chamber where no party has a majority; it is the situation that makes coalitions necessary, not the cabinet itself.
entries.definitionCN: 没有任何政党过半的议会；它是促成联合政府的局面，而不是内阁本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin picture, the real word family and the real political phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语画面、真实的同族词与真实的政治说法。

normal.en: Co- 'together' plus a root meaning 'grow': two parties growing into one trunk.
normal.cn: 表示「共同」的前缀加表示「生长」的词根：两个政党长成一根主干。

normal.en: The family runs coalition, coalesce, coalescence, coalitionist and coalitional.
normal.cn: 同族词包括表示联合的名词、表示合并的动词、表示合并过程的名词，以及联合派与联盟形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the trade: form a coalition government, a grand coalition government, a caretaker coalition government.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出这一行当：组成联合政府、大联合政府、看守联合政府。

normal.en: Historical anchor: the Fox-North ministry of 1783 was already called a coalition, long before the phrase became ordinary.
normal.cn: 历史锚点：一七八三年的福克斯与诺斯内阁已被称作联合政府，远早于这个短语变得平常。

normal.en: Arithmetic anchor: majority and minority coalitions differ by seats, grand coalitions by the size of the partners.
normal.cn: 算术锚点：多数与少数联合政府差在席位，大联合政府差在伙伴的体量。

abstract.en: Two chairs face away from each other until someone turns both toward one table.
abstract.cn: 两把椅子本来背对着，直到有人把它们一起转向同一张桌子。

abstract.en: A post list is circled in two colours of ink, and every name carries two signatures.
abstract.cn: 一张职位名单被两种颜色的墨水圈过，每个名字后面都有两个签名。

abstract.en: A borrowed car with two drivers: it moves, but both hands sit on the wheel.
abstract.cn: 一辆借来的车有两个司机：车能走，但方向盘上有两双手。

examples.en: The coalition government fell when the junior partner withdrew its ministers.
examples.cn: 小党撤回部长后，联合政府垮台了。

examples.en: Economists warned that a coalition government would struggle to pass a budget.
examples.cn: 经济学家警告说，联合政府将难以通过预算。

examples.en: She covered the coalition government for a regional paper.
examples.cn: 她为一家地区报纸报道这届联合政府。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「科阿利申·政府」——谐音「合力伸」：各党把力气合起来，伸到同一张桌子上办事 → 联合政府

root: 拉丁 coalescere「长到一起」= co-（共同）+ alescere「生长」，源自 alere「滋养」；名词经法语进入英语，政府义为十九世纪后的政治用法。短语后半出自拉丁 gubernare「掌舵」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bargain: parties grow together, sign a programme, meet as a body, hold office for a term, and then vary by seats, by the size of the partners, by how long the deal lasts and by the level of government.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一笔交易展开：各党长到一起、签下纲领、作为班子开会、执政一个任期，随后再按席位多寡、伙伴体量、协议时长与政府层级分化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate parties grow into one cabinet, then hold office until the seam shows.
core.cn: 核心意象：分开的政党长成一个内阁，然后执政到接缝暴露。

branches.en: THE DEAL AND ITS WEAK FORM: a signed fusion, and the version that survives without half the seats.
branches.cn: 协议与弱势版本：签约合并，以及席位不到半数仍能存活的那种。

branches.en: BODY AND BIG TWO: a weekly cabinet meeting, and the crisis version built from the largest rivals.
branches.cn: 班子与两大党：每周开会的内阁，以及由最大对手在危机中搭成的那种。

branches.en: FULL TERM AND STOPGAP: a term that runs its course, and a term with an expiry date set by the next election.
branches.cn: 完整任期与过渡任期：走完全程的任期，以及把到期日定在下一次选举的任期。

branches.en: MAJORITY: seats beyond half make the partnership self-sufficient.
branches.cn: 多数：席位过半使伙伴关系自足。

branches.en: LOCAL: the same device in a council or devolved assembly, scaled down but identical in logic.
branches.cn: 地方层面：同一装置用于市议会或下放议会，规模缩小而逻辑相同。

intro.en: The phrase is a noun plus a noun, and both halves are built from Latin pieces that also form many other English words.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个名词合成，而两半都由拉丁语构件搭起，这些构件还构成许多别的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Coalescere supplies the first noun through its participle; gubernare supplies the second through French; the suffixes -ition and -ment turn actions into nouns.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词「长到一起」经其分词提供第一个名词；拉丁动词「掌舵」经法语提供第二个名词的动词；表示动作的名词后缀把动作变成名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示「共同、一起」的前缀
items.example: The prefix binds two separate things into one act.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把分开的两样东西绑进同一个动作。

items.structure: co- + alescere (Latin root, 'to begin to grow')
items.meaningCN: 表示「生长、开始生长」的词根
items.example: The root pictures a shoot putting out new wood.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根画出新枝抽出新木的画面。

items.meaningCN: 表示「动作或其结果」的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix turns the act of fusing into a countable noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「合并」这一动作变成可数名词。

items.meaning: a union of parties or groups
items.meaningCN: 党派或团体结成的联合体
items.example: The coalition held together for a full term.
items.exampleCN: 这个联合体撑满了整个任期。

items.meaning: the body that runs a state
items.meaningCN: 治理国家的机构
items.example: The government published its spending plans.
items.exampleCN: 政府公布了支出计划。

items.structure: govern (verb base, from Latin gubernare 'to steer')
items.meaningCN: 掌舵；治理
items.example: Coalitions govern by compromise.
items.exampleCN: 联合政府靠妥协来治理。

items.meaning: result or means of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示「动作的结果或手段」的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix makes the act of steering into an institution.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「掌舵」的动作变成一种机构。

items.meaningCN: 主张多党联合执政的人
items.example: The coalitionist defended the deal to both party boards.
items.exampleCN: 这位联合派向两个党的执委会为这笔协议辩护。

items.meaningCN: 与联合体相关的
items.example: Coalitional discipline held through the budget vote.
items.exampleCN: 联合体的纪律在预算表决中维持住了。

items.meaningCN: 政府的；由政府行使的
items.example: The governmental reshuffle followed the election.
items.exampleCN: 选举之后发生了政府改组。

items.meaningCN: 政府之间的
items.example: An intergovernmental panel reviewed the plan.
items.exampleCN: 一个政府间小组审查了该计划。

definition_zh: 自由主义；经济自由主义；文化宽容立场；古典自由主义；现代社会自由主义；宗教自由主义；国际主义取向；贬义的放任标签
definition_en: a political tradition that puts individual freedom first and asks how far the state may limit it
core_image: 一个人推开挡在面前的门，门后没有人为他规定路线，只有一块空地写着「自行选择」
scene: 旧政论小册子摊在桌上，作者先主张人应当自己判断，再主张掌权者应当少插手，后来的人把这两句话合成一套主张。Modern liberalism grew out of a demand for individual freedom and limited power.
sceneCN: 旧政论小册子摊在桌上，作者先主张人应当自己判断，再主张掌权者应当少插手，后来的人把这两句话合成一套主张；句中的词指「以个人自由为核心的政治思想传统」（第 1 个义项：把个人自由视为最高政治价值、并据此讨论政府权限的思想传统）。图中可辨识物件：小册子、行间批注、摊开的书页、压住纸角的镇纸。

pos.zh: 自由主义（不可数，指思想传统）
自由主义的一种具体主张或流派（可数）

senses.title: The tradition that puts freedom first
senses.titleCN: 以个人自由为首要价值的思想传统
senses.definition: a political tradition holding that individuals should decide their own lives and that state power must be justified and limited
senses.definitionCN: 主张个人应自行决定生活、国家权力必须被说明理由并受限制的政治思想传统
senses.example: Liberalism treats personal choice as the default, not as a privilege granted by the state.
senses.exampleCN: 自由主义把个人选择视为默认状态，而不是国家授予的特权。
senses.why: The Latin root means 'free', and the adjective built on it first described a free person rather than a slave; the doctrine turns that status into a principle of government.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「自由」，由它构成的形容词最初形容自由人而非奴隶；这套主张把那种身份提升为治理原则。

senses.title: The economic wing: markets before planners
senses.titleCN: 经济一支：市场优先于计划
senses.definition: the strand that trusts markets, contracts and private property and distrusts tariffs, subsidies and state direction of industry
senses.definitionCN: 信任市场、契约与私有财产，怀疑关税、补贴与国家指导产业的那一支
senses.example: Economic liberalism argues that prices set by trade carry more information than any ministry can.
senses.exampleCN: 经济自由主义主张，由交易形成的价格所携带的信息多于任何部委所能掌握的。
senses.why: If individuals know their own interests best, the same argument applies to buying and selling, so the doctrine extends from persons to prices.
senses.whyCN: 如果个人最清楚自己的利益，同一道理也适用于买卖，于是这套主张从个人延伸到价格。

senses.title: The cultural wing: tolerance as a habit
senses.titleCN: 文化一支：把宽容当作习惯
senses.definition: the outlook that treats unusual beliefs, tastes and lifestyles as matters for the individual rather than for the law
senses.definitionCN: 把非主流的信念、品味与生活方式视为个人事务而非法律事务的立场
senses.example: Social liberalism shows in small things: who may marry, dress or worship without asking permission.
senses.exampleCN: 社会自由主义体现在小事上：谁可以不经过许可就结婚、穿着或礼拜。
senses.why: Freedom of thought is useless if it stops at the skull; the doctrine therefore pushes the same principle into custom and law.
senses.whyCN: 思想自由若止于头骨之内便毫无用处；因此这套主张把同一原则推进到习俗与法律之中。

senses.title: The older programme: small state, firm law
senses.titleCN: 较早的纲领：小政府、硬法治
senses.definition: the nineteenth-century programme of limited government, secure property, free trade and equality before the law
senses.definitionCN: 十九世纪那套纲领：有限政府、财产保障、自由贸易与法律面前人人平等
senses.example: Classical liberalism wanted the state to keep order and then step back.
senses.exampleCN: 古典自由主义希望国家维持秩序，然后退到一旁。
senses.why: The first liberals fought absolute monarchs, so their freedom meant a state that could not reach into a household at will.
senses.whyCN: 最早的自由派对抗的是绝对君主，因此他们的自由意味着国家不能随意伸手进人家门。

senses.title: The newer programme: freedom with a floor
senses.titleCN: 较晚的纲领：自由加上底线保障
senses.definition: the twentieth-century version that uses public schooling, health care and insurance to make freedom real for people without money
senses.definitionCN: 二十世纪版本：用公共教育、医疗与保险，使没有钱的人也真正享有自由
senses.example: Modern liberalism accepts a welfare state as the condition of personal independence.
senses.exampleCN: 现代社会自由主义把福利国家当作个人独立的条件。
senses.why: A person who cannot afford to refuse a bad job is not free in practice, so the doctrine widened from permission to capacity.
senses.whyCN: 一个无法拒绝糟糕工作的人，在实践中并不自由；于是这套主张从「允许」扩展到「有能力」。

senses.title: The religious wing: reason inside faith
senses.titleCN: 宗教一支：信仰内部运用理性
senses.definition: the movement that reads scripture through history and reason and defends the right to interpret it personally
senses.definitionCN: 以历史与理性解读经文、并维护个人解释权的那场运动
senses.example: Religious liberalism argued that a creed kept by argument is stronger than one kept by police.
senses.exampleCN: 宗教自由主义主张，靠论证维持的信条比靠警察维持的更强。
senses.why: The principle of private judgement does not stop at politics; applied to scripture it produces a liberal form of faith.
senses.whyCN: 私人判断的原则不会止步于政治；用在经文上，就生出一种自由主义的信仰形态。

senses.title: The outward face: trade, law and rights abroad
senses.titleCN: 面向外部：对外贸易、国际法与人权
senses.definition: the outlook that prefers open trade, international institutions and the protection of foreigners' rights to closed borders
senses.definitionCN: 偏好开放贸易、国际机构与保护外侨权利、而非封闭边境的立场
senses.example: Liberalism abroad meant treaties, arbitration and the belief that commerce follows law.
senses.exampleCN: 对外的自由主义意味着条约、仲裁，以及商业随法律而行的信念。
senses.why: If freedom belongs to persons rather than to tribes, borders cannot be the end of the argument.
senses.whyCN: 如果自由属于个人而非部族，边境就不能成为论证的终点。

senses.title: The dismissive use: soft, vague, unrealistic
senses.titleCN: 贬义用法：软弱、含糊、不切实际
senses.definition: a hostile label for policies said to avoid hard choices and to dissolve responsibilities into permissiveness
senses.definitionCN: 带敌意的标签，用来指回避艰难选择、把责任消解为放任的政策
senses.example: Critics used liberalism as a sneer, meaning a refusal ever to say no.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把自由主义当讽刺语用，意思是从不肯说「不」。
senses.why: Any word naming a side in a quarrel will be used as a weapon by the other side; the sneer keeps the name but drops the argument.
senses.whyCN: 任何为争论一方命名的词都会被另一方当武器使用；这种讥讽保留了名称，却抽掉了论证。

intro.en: The chain is clear: Latin liber 'free' gave liberalis 'of a free person, generous', French made libéralisme, and English took the political label in the early nineteenth century. The formal derivation is not in doubt, though the political meaning arrived late.
intro.cn: 这条链是清楚的：拉丁语中表示「自由的」形容词衍生出表示「自由人的、慷慨的」形容词，法语再加名词后缀构成一套主张的名称，英语在十九世纪早期借入这一政治标签。形式上的衍生并无不确定之处，只是政治义出现得晚。

items.en: Liber, libera, liberum meant 'free', said of a person who was not a slave, and also 'free from restraint'. The same root yields liberty through libertas.
items.cn: 这个拉丁形容词意为「自由的」，用来形容不是奴隶的人，也指不受约束；同一词根经表示「自由」的名词衍生出英语中的自由一词。

items.en: Liberalis first meant 'belonging to a free person' and then 'generous, open-handed', because a free man was expected to give freely.
items.cn: 这个拉丁形容词先指「属于自由人的」，再指「慷慨、大方」，因为自由人被认为应当乐于给予。

items.en: Libertas 'freedom' was already a political word in Rome, used of the rights of a citizen against arbitrary power; English liberty comes from it.
items.cn: 拉丁语中表示「自由」的名词在罗马已是政治用语，指公民对抗任意权力的权利；英语中的自由一词即由它而来。

items.en: In France libéralisme named the views of those who wanted a constitution and a parliament, not absolute rule; the label was given by opponents as often as it was claimed.
items.cn: 在法国，这个词指主张宪法与议会、反对绝对统治者的那套观点；这个标签既常由对手加给他们，也常由同路人自称。

items.en: English took the noun in the early nineteenth century, first as a foreign label for continental politics and soon as a domestic one; by the eighteen-thirties it named a recognised side in Parliament.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪早期借入这个名词，先是作为描述欧陆政治的外来标签，很快也用于本国；到三十年代，它已指议会中一个被承认的阵营。

items.en: In the twentieth century American usage made liberalism the label of the welfare-state left, while many European parties kept it for free-market views, so the same word now points in two directions.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，美式用法把这个词当成福利国家左翼的标签，而欧洲许多党派仍用它指自由市场主张，于是同一个词指向两个方向。

note.en: The first group shares a root or a shape with the headword; the second group holds ideas that sit close in debate but are not interchangeable.
note.cn: 第一组与词条同根或形近；第二组是论辩中挨得很近、却不能互换的主张。

entries.tag: same root, a state not a doctrine
entries.definition: Liberty names the condition of being free, for one person or in a constitution; a doctrine, a party and a programme need the longer noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指自由的状态，可属个人也可属宪法；而一套主张、一个党派与一份纲领要用那个更长的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective, and its noun for a person; it describes a position or a policy, while the headword names the whole tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，也可作名词指人；它描述某种立场或政策，而词条指整个思想传统。

entries.definition: Generosity or openness of mind, a personal quality; it is not a political doctrine, though it shares the root.
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨或心胸开阔，属个人品质；虽同词根，却不是政治主张。

entries.definition: Originally a freed slave, later a person without moral restraint; the freedom here is personal conduct, not public order.
entries.definitionCN: 原指被释放的奴隶，后指不受道德约束的人；这里的自由属个人行为，无关公共秩序。

entries.definition: A tradition that wants reform to remove old privileges; it overlaps with modern liberalism but puts more stress on collective progress.
entries.definitionCN: 主张以改革清除旧特权的传统；它与现代一支有重叠，但更强调集体进步。

entries.definition: It takes freedom to mean almost no state at all, including low tax and few laws; classical liberals stop well short of that.
entries.definitionCN: 把自由理解为几乎没有国家，包括低税与极少法律；古典一支远没有走到这一步。

entries.definition: A movement that seeks equality through elections and welfare within a market economy; it shares aims with modern liberalism but grew from a labour base.
entries.definitionCN: 主张在市场经济的框架内通过选举与福利追求平等；它与现代一支目标相近，但出身于劳工阵营。

entries.definition: The policy of leaving trade alone; it is one economic rule that liberals may adopt, not the whole tradition.
entries.definitionCN: 不干预交易的政策；它是自由派可能采纳的一条经济规则，而非整套传统。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin root, the real word family and the real political phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的政治说法。

normal.en: The Latin root means 'free'; the adjective built on it first described a free person, not a policy.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁词根意为「自由」；由它构成的形容词最初形容自由人，而不是形容政策。

normal.en: The family runs liberal, liberty, liberality, libertarian and liberalize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括表示自由的形容词、表示自由的名词、表示慷慨的名词、自由至上主义者与使自由化。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the argument: classical liberalism, economic liberalism, modern liberalism.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出这场争论：古典一支、经济一支、现代一支。

normal.en: Note the suffix: the system of ideas takes the doctrine suffix, while the person takes the plain adjective.
normal.cn: 注意后缀：成套观念用表示「主张」的后缀，指人则用那个普通形容词。

normal.en: History anchor: the label was first used against people who wanted a constitution, then adopted by them.
normal.cn: 历史锚点：这个标签先被用来指称主张宪法的人，后来又被他们自己采用。

abstract.en: A door opens onto empty ground: no route drawn, only the instruction to choose one.
abstract.cn: 一扇门开向空地：没有画好的路线，只有「自己选一条」的指示。

abstract.en: A hand holds a fence post upright but does not push the walker.
abstract.cn: 一只手扶正篱笆桩，却不推着行人往前走。

abstract.en: Two maps of one city, one marked with permission, the other with capacity.
abstract.cn: 同一座城市的两张地图，一张标着「允许」，一张标着「有能力」。

examples.en: Liberalism insists that a majority may not simply silence a minority.
examples.cn: 这套主张坚持，多数不能就这样让少数闭嘴。

examples.en: Economic liberalism shaped the trade treaties of the nineteenth century.
examples.cn: 经济自由主义塑造了十九世纪的贸易条约。

examples.en: The essay traces liberalism from a protest slogan to a governing creed.
examples.cn: 这篇文章梳理了它从抗议口号变成执政信条的过程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「利伯若利泽姆」——谐音「理不论」：凡事讲理、不问出身，人人自己作主 → 自由主义

root: 拉丁 liber「自由的」+ 形容词后缀 -alis 构成 liberalis「自由人的、慷慨的」，再加名词后缀 -ismus 成学派名，经法语进入英语；同源名词 libertas「自由」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses show one principle spreading: freedom as a status, then as an economic rule, a cultural habit, an old programme, a newer programme, a way of reading scripture, a foreign policy and finally a term of abuse.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项展示同一条原则扩散：自由先是身份，再是经济规则、文化习惯、较早的纲领、较晚的纲领、读经方式、对外政策，最后沦为骂人的词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person allowed to choose a route, then a state that must justify every fence.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人被允许自己选路；接着是国家必须为每一道篱笆说明理由。

branches.en: PRINCIPLE AND ITS INWARD FORM: freedom as the founding value, and the same argument applied inside a faith.
branches.cn: 原则与其内向形态：自由作为奠基价值，以及同一论证用在信仰内部。

branches.en: THE STATE'S HAND: light in the market, heavy in welfare, both argued from the same freedom.
branches.cn: 国家之手：在市场里轻，在福利上重，两者都由同一种自由推出。

branches.en: OPENNESS OUTWARD: tolerance at home and treaties abroad come from one refusal to police others.
branches.cn: 向外的开放：对内的宽容与对外的条约，都源于不肯管束他人。

branches.en: OLD PROGRAMME: small government, firm law, secure property.
branches.cn: 旧纲领：小政府、硬法治、财产保障。

branches.en: SNEAR: the same name used as a weapon by the other side.
branches.cn: 讥称：同一个名字被对方当武器使用。

intro.en: The word is a Latin root plus an adjective suffix plus a doctrine suffix, and each piece also builds other common English words.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁词根、形容词后缀与表示主张的名词后缀依次搭成，每一部分还能构成别的常用英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin liber supplies the root and libertas supplies the related noun; -alis makes the adjective and -ismus makes the name of the school.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「自由」的词提供词根，其同源名词提供相关名词；形容词后缀构成形容词，表示主张的名词后缀构成学派名称。

items.meaningCN: 表示「自由、不受束缚」的词根
items.example: The root names the status of a person who is not a slave.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指不是奴隶的那种身份。

items.meaningCN: 表示「属于……的」的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表示归属的形容词。

items.meaningCN: 表示「体系、做法或主张」的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix turns a viewpoint into the name of a movement.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把一种看法变成一场运动的名称。

items.meaningCN: 自由的；开放的；慷慨的
items.example: A liberal order leaves room for disagreement.
items.exampleCN: 一种自由的秩序为分歧留出空间。

items.meaningCN: 建立在自由之上的那套主张
items.example: Liberalism arrived with the demand for a written constitution.
items.exampleCN: 这套主张随制定成文宪法的要求一同到来。

items.meaningCN: 慷慨；心胸开阔
items.example: Her liberality with time surprised the committee.
items.exampleCN: 她舍得花时间，令委员会惊讶。

items.meaningCN: 不开明的；不宽容的
items.example: The illiberal clause banned public meetings.
items.exampleCN: 那条规定不宽容的条款禁止了公众集会。

items.meaning: one who wants the state kept to a minimum
items.meaningCN: 主张把国家压到最小的人
items.example: A libertarian would abolish the licence altogether.
items.exampleCN: 自由至上主义者会干脆取消这项许可。

items.meaning: to make freer or less restricted
items.meaningCN: 使更自由、减少限制
items.example: They liberalized the rules on imported books.
items.exampleCN: 他们放宽了进口书籍的规定。

items.meaningCN: 放宽限制的过程
items.example: Trade liberalization lowered the price of cloth.
items.exampleCN: 贸易自由化压低了布匹价格。
